facts.value: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 at max effort through Claude Code on the first-party API, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 43, 39 and 43 of 105 (repo 1: 18, 17, 22 of 45 - repo 2: 25, 22, 21 of 60). Mean 41.7, spread 4. *** THIS SUPERSEDES OPUS 5.5 (MAX EFFORT) - MEAN OF 2 (41.0 OF 105) *** *** WHY THE REPLICATES EXIST *** the first pass measured this ladder at one run per rung and it came out monotone - medium 30, high 32, xhigh 35, max 43. That was suggestive and nothing more: no gap in it exceeded the 13-point spread this board has measured between two runs of ONE identical max-effort configuration, so the ordering of any two adjacent rungs was unresolved and every note said so. Three runs per rung is what can resolve it, and the whole ladder is being re-measured that way rather than only its top. The board currently reads low 22.3 (n=3), medium 30.3 (n=3), high 31.7 (n=3), xhigh 36 (n=3), max 41.7 (n=3). *** THE REPLICATES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE FIRST RUN *** same model string claude-opus-5-5[1m], same effort, same timeout, same price table, same blind judge. Only the arm name differs, so the spread above is run-to-run variance and nothing else. *** WALL AND COST *** Walls 68.5, 60.0, 72.2 minutes, mean 66.9; cost $60.49, $58.39, $56.69, mean $58.52. COST IS A LIST ESTIMATE at Anthropic's published Opus 5.5 rates - $4 input, $20 output, $0.20 cache read (a 0.05x cache multiplier unique to this model, where every other model here uses 0.1x) and $8 cache write, the 1-hour rate, which is what this harness actually writes and what the streams confirm. Not an invoice, hence `list`. *** GENUINE EXTRAS *** 9, 9 and 9 across the runs, mean 9.0 - real defects found in the repos that nobody planted, reported separately and never folded into the score. *** THE CONTEXT WINDOW *** every run here holds a 1M window and crosses zero compaction boundaries, so these rows compare cleanly to each other and NOT to the Opus 5 ladder, which ran the CLI's default 200K and compacted repeatedly mid-task. Autocompact ran at the CLI's own default throughout. *** RECEIPTS *** All legs exited 0, run SEQUENTIALLY, one repo at a time. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 on every leg - an OpenAI model scoring an Anthropic one, so neither the model itself nor a sibling of it. The runs shared the laptop with legs from other vendors, which the wall marker discloses; scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: The clearest null on the board's Anthropic dial: Sonnet 5 at max scores 9/105, exactly what the default-effort Sonnet 5 row scored. facts.value: Fable 5.1's dial does not run in a straight line: medium scores 21/105, BELOW its own low row (29) and well below high (33) and max (43). The run is clean - both legs exited success, no truncation, no permission denials, no tool errors - and the raw captures say why in the tool mix rather than in the thinking. At medium the model worked almost entirely through the shell: 83 Bash calls against 3 Reads and ZERO Edits or Greps on repo 1, and 99 Bash against 2 Reads and zero Edits on repo 2. At low it read the codebase instead - 44 Reads, 20 Greps, 16 Edits on repo 1. That shows up in the billing shape too: medium pulled 4.0M cached-read tokens on repo 1 against low's 19.7M, because a session that never reads files into context keeps a small context to re-send. Fewer bugs found is what you would expect from a model that barely looked at the code.

facts.value: Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 at low effort through Claude Code on the first-party API, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 20, 17 and 20 of 105 (repo 1: 7, 6, 7 - repo 2: 13, 11, 13). Mean 19.0, range 3. *** THIS SUPERSEDES SONNET 5.5 (LOW EFFORT) (20 OF 105) *** *** THE REPLICATES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE FIRST RUN *** same model string, effort, timeout, price table and blind judge; only the arm name differs, so the spread is run-to-run variance. For comparison the board currently publishes Sonnet 5 at max effort 9, Sonnet 5 at high effort 9, Opus 5.5 at low effort 22.3 (mean of 3) of 105. *** WALL AND COST *** walls 7.4, 9.7, 8.4 minutes, mean 8.5; cost $5.75, $6.20, $5.25, mean $5.73. *** GENUINE EXTRAS *** 5, 12 and 7 across the runs, mean 8.0, never folded into the score. *** HOW IT SPENT THE RUN *** On repo 1 it took 52, 39, 44 turns (the harness's own count); it first wrote its report 3, 5, 4 minutes in and its last model call came at minute 3, 5, 4. For scale: Opus 5.5 at low took 51-64 turns there over three runs of 4-5 minutes, and every one of those runs wrote its report within 1 minute of its last call. On repo 2 it took 67, 58, 39 turns (the harness's own count); it first wrote its report 4, 4, 4 minutes in and its last model call came at minute 4, 4, 4. For scale: Opus 5.5 at low took 58-86 turns there over three runs of 5-8 minutes, and every one of those runs wrote its report within 1 minute of its last call. *** SAME MACHINE AS THE OPUS 5.5 LADDER *** configured byte-identical to the opus55* arms except the model slug and the effort flag: Claude Code straight onto Anthropic's first-party API, no proxy, 1M window requested with the [1m] suffix, CLI-default autocompact, same prompt, same timeout class, same blind judge. The two Sonnet 5 rows on this board ran older Claude Code builds (2.1.218, 2.1.267) and compacted mid-task - 5 compactions across their 4 legs, peaks 284,197 to 295,210 tokens - so a gap against them mixes the model version with how much of each run's context survived, and is not a clean version delta. Effort is a first-party Claude Code tier (documented enum low|medium|high|xhigh|max, enforced: an invented tier is answered 'Unknown --effort value'), taken at face value like every other Claude row here. The harness stated init.model claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] on every leg - the [1m] suffix honoured, so this is a 1M-window run - on Claude Code 2.1.283. Peak context 360,079 tokens; 0 compactions across 6 legs. Autocompact ran at the CLI default. *** COST IS A LIST ESTIMATE *** token counts at Anthropic's published Sonnet 5.5 rates (as read 2026-09-28): $2 input, $10 output, $0.20 cache read, $4 cache write - the 1-hour rate, which is what this harness writes. The harness's own cost figure is NOT a cross-check on this model: Claude Code reported its cost basis for Sonnet 5.5 as 'unknown' and priced the run on Opus 5.5's table - its figure is exactly those tokens at Opus 5.5 rates, about a fifth higher than Sonnet 5.5's own. So the check here is on tokens: each leg's metered counts agree with the harness's own per-model counts within 3 per cent. Claude Code on a subscription exposes no invoice, hence `list`. *** RECEIPTS *** All legs exited 0 with a report written, run SEQUENTIALLY, one repo at a time. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 - an OpenAI model scoring an Anthropic one, so neither the model itself nor a sibling of it. 3 of the 6 legs shared the laptop with another arm and the rest had it to themselves, which the wall marker discloses per leg - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 at xhigh effort through Claude Code on the first-party API, released 2026-10-07 and run the same day. MEAN OF THREE RUNS of one configuration: 16, 19 and 20 of 105 (repo 1: 6, 8 and 13 of 45 - repo 2: 10, 11 and 7 of 60), mean 18.3. Genuine unplanted extras 10, 5 and 5; claimed-only fixes 2, 0 and 0. Walls 22.7, 20.5 and 29.1 minutes; cost $4.50, $4.30 and $5.59. *** EFFORT, READ OFF THE WIRE *** Claude Code 2.1.292 does not know this model yet (it logs it as unrecognized), so the request was captured rather than the CLI taken at its word: the main loop sends effort xhigh with adaptive thinking to claude-haiku-5-5, with the 1M-context header, and the API accepts it. Claude Code's one per-session title call runs at high, which the effort flag does not reach; the tier describes the main loop. A first-party tier, accepted, not magnitude-probed; not the ceiling (max exists). *** COST IS PRICED PER REQUEST *** Haiku 5.5 is billed by each request's prompt length: $0.10 input / $0.20 1-hour cache write / $0.01 cache read / $0.50 output per million tokens up to a 100,000-token prompt, and $0.50 / $1 / $0.05 / $2.50 above it, every token of the request at its prompt's tier. Claude Code's instructions and tools alone are about 50,000 tokens, so the conversation crosses the line within a few turns: 552 of the 587 requests across the six legs were priced at the upper tier. Each request was priced from Claude Code's own session record, because the CLI's cost table has no entry for this model. 98.6% of prompt tokens were cache reads. A list estimate, not a bill. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0, run strictly one at a time on one account. The machine was otherwise idle for every leg, so the wall figures compare directly against other uncontended rows. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.quote: id: Haiku 4.5 - mean of 2 | caveat: Mean of two runs (1 and 2 of 105). Haiku 4.5 has no effort setting - it uses a thinking-token budget, and Claude Code always sets it to 31,999 tokens - so the effort column reads default. Cost is a list estimate.

facts.value: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5, October 2025, 200K context) through Claude Code on the first-party API. MEAN OF TWO RUNS of one configuration: 1 and 2 of 105 (repo 1: 1 and 0 of 45 - repo 2: 0 and 2 of 60), mean 1.5. Claimed-only fixes 0 and 1; genuine unplanted extras 3 and 2. Walls 18.6 and 15.2 minutes; cost $1.91 and $2.53. *** NO EFFORT SETTING EXISTS FOR THIS MODEL *** Anthropic's Haiku 4.5 page lists default effort as 'Not supported' and thinking as 'Extended': the model takes a thinking-token budget, not an effort level, and the effort documentation's list of supported models includes Haiku 5.5 but not 4.5. Claude Code follows that: read off the wire, --effort xhigh and --effort low send identical requests - no effort field, and extended thinking at budget_tokens 31,999, the most the CLI's 32,000-token output cap allows. So this is Haiku 4.5 exactly as Claude Code runs it for every user, at the CLI's maximum thinking budget; the row is labelled default, not with an effort tier. *** RECEIPTS *** 98.0% of prompt tokens were cache reads; list rates $1 input / $2 1-hour cache write / $0.10 cache read / $5 output per MTok, priced per request from Claude Code's session record. A list estimate, not a bill. All four legs ran at the same time on one account, and each leg's scores and priced responses were checked to come from its own stream alone, with none shared among the four. Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Superseded 2026-09-16 by the n=2 MEAN row at the same setting (43.5). This row is one of the two runs behind it and is kept as a receipt. Read its 42 with care: it is the 2026-07-31 judge pass, which recorded its judge as grok-4.5 and had no served-model field at all. facts.value: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 (4): EFFORT IS INERT ON THIS ROW, measured at last. It shipped verified_ceiling, was corrected to first_party on 09-11, and is now inert_default with effort 'default' - the same label every other aggregator-routed row on this board carries. A nine-runs-per-condition probe on the exact surface this arm used (OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages, receipts results/effort-dial-probes/20260912-qwen38max-openrouter-anthropic.txt and 20260912-qwen38max-all-n9.txt) puts reasoning.effort=low at mean 13,017 output tokens (7,897-16,402), reasoning.effort=high at 14,815 (11,524-20,237), and NO effort field at all at 13,622 (9,179-19,757) - a 1.14x spread between the tiers against a 2.15x worst within-condition spread, with every range overlapping every other. The field does nothing; the run sat at Alibaba's own default either way. SELF-CORRECTION, same day: for a few hours this note also said the shim had caused the problem by deleting Anthropic's native 'thinking' field to install 'reasoning.effort', on the strength of that field measuring very differently (mean 5,468). That rested on ONE budget value, which can only show a field is read, not that it binds. A three-value probe (receipt results/effort-dial-probes/20260912-qwen38max-budget-scaling-openrouter.txt, n=3 each) put budget_tokens=2,000 at mean 5,627 output tokens, 8,000 at 4,735 and 24,000 at 4,111 - twelve times the budget moved the mean 0.73x, the wrong way, inside a 1.95x worst within-condition spread. So budget_tokens is a switch rather than a dial on this path, and the switch SUPPRESSES: sending it in any form costs about two thirds of the model's thinking against the 13,622 no-field baseline. That makes the shim's pop the configuration producing the MOST thinking available here, not a discarded control - with 'thinking' gone and reasoning.effort inert, the request fell through to the endpoint default, which is exactly what inert_default records. The label is unaffected; only the causal story changed, and the shims were reverted to dropping the field. A control on Alibaba's own endpoint shows native thinking landing far higher there and fully overlapping Alibaba's own no-field baseline, so the suppression is a property of the aggregator hop and not of the model. RE-MEASURED AT n=6 AND THEN n=9 the same day, because a claim this size should not rest on three samples (receipt results/effort-dial-probes/20260912-qwen38max-all-n9.txt, 24 fresh concurrent calls pooled with the originals and the n=6 top-ups; every condition on both routes now stands at nine runs, so no verdict rests on a smaller sample than the one it is compared against): through OpenRouter budget_tokens=24,000 gives mean 4,967 (3,568-7,637) against a no-field baseline of 13,622 (9,179-19,757); straight to Alibaba the same field gives 13,168 (9,185-15,977) against 14,379 (11,586-17,442). All verdicts survive - cross-route 2.65x against a 2.15x worst within-cell spread, ranges disjoint, the field costing 64% of the thinking through the hop and nothing at all direct. The effort WORD reads more inert at nine runs than at three: low-vs-high means 1.14x through OpenRouter and 1.04x direct, ranges fully overlapping. The bigger samples did move one number: the OpenRouter no-field baseline measured 15,714 at n=3, 13,339 at n=6 and 13,622 at n=9 - three samples had overestimated it by 15%, and the six- and nine-run readings agree to 2%. Quote the nine-run figures only. Ranges can only widen with n, so each pass was a test the finding could fail. Still at n=3 and flagged as such: the three-value budget sweep, whose top-up was attempted the same day and blocked when the OpenRouter account ran out of credits mid-series - read the RANKING of the three budgets as unmeasured; the suppression claim does not depend on it. The scores, cost and wall are unchanged. EARLIER CORRECTIONS, 2026-09-11, on three counts, while adding the Qwen3.8-Flash rows. (1) HARNESS. This row was published as 'Claude Code / Alibaba API'. It never called Alibaba's API. The arm ran through a local pass-through shim with upstream=OpenRouter's qwen3.8-max slug, so the path was Claude Code -> local proxy -> OpenRouter -> Alibaba, exactly like the Kimi K3, Ox Alpha and GLM-5.3 rows, all of which correctly say 'Claude Code / OpenRouter'. This row was the only OR-routed row on the board claiming a direct vendor API. (2) EFFORT STATUS. It was published verified_ceiling. No probe receipt exists - the only Qwen file in results/effort-dial-probes is the 2026-09-11 Flash one. The claim rested on QwenCloud's documented enum (low|medium|xhigh, default xhigh, high->xhigh) plus a check that thinking was live (248 thinking blocks across the raw logs). Under this board's own vocabulary that is first_party - a documented tier taken at face value - because verified_ceiling requires a probe that SEPARATES the levels. The row's own note also argued that Alibaba validates effort 'while OR accepts any string and applies none', which cannot both be true of a request routed through OR; whether the effort field survived the proxy and the aggregator to reach Alibaba was never established. (3) COST, $31.10 -> $33.30. The arm modelled cache writes as FREE. OpenRouter lists qwen3.8-max-0902 cache writes at $2.50/MTok and this run wrote 879,902 cache-creation tokens. A sweep of OR's listing found Qwen is the ONLY family on this board it charges a cache-write fee for - DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, Tencent and Meta publish none - so $0.00 is right on every other aggregator-routed arm and was wrong only here. The SCORES are unchanged; only the two labels and the cost move. And a caveat larger than the correction: 12.94% of this row's prompt tokens (8,282,777 of them, $16.57 - HALF the row) were billed as uncached input, against 0.002% on the two Flash rows running the same harness against Alibaba's own endpoint. That ~5,000x gap in cache-miss rate is a property of the proxy-plus-aggregator path, not of the model, so read this row's cost as a cost OF THAT PATH rather than a price for Qwen3.8-Max. NOT re-probed on purpose: the Aug 3 arm used an unlisted qwen3.8-max slug and what OpenRouter lists now is qwen3.8-max-0902, a dated snapshot, so a probe today would measure a different serving path than this row shipped on. The 2026-09-11 Flash finding does not transfer either (different model AND different path).

Under this board's own vocabulary that is first_party - a documented tier taken at face value - because verified_ceiling requires a probe that SEPARATES the levels. The row's own note also argued that Alibaba validates effort 'while OR accepts any string and applies none', which cannot both be true of a request routed through OR; whether the effort field survived the proxy and the aggregator to reach Alibaba was never established. (3) COST, $31.10 -> $33.30. The arm modelled cache writes as FREE. OpenRouter lists qwen3.8-max-0902 cache writes at $2.50/MTok and this run wrote 879,902 cache-creation tokens. A sweep of OR's listing found Qwen is the ONLY family on this board it charges a cache-write fee for - DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, Tencent and Meta publish none - so $0.00 is right on every other aggregator-routed arm and was wrong only here. The SCORES are unchanged; only the two labels and the cost move. And a caveat larger than the correction: 12.94% of this row's prompt tokens (8,282,777 of them, $16.57 - HALF the row) were billed as uncached input, against 0.002% on the two Flash rows running the same harness against Alibaba's own endpoint. That ~5,000x gap in cache-miss rate is a property of the proxy-plus-aggregator path, not of the model, so read this row's cost as a cost OF THAT PATH rather than a price for Qwen3.8-Max. NOT re-probed on purpose: the Aug 3 arm used an unlisted qwen3.8-max slug and what OpenRouter lists now is qwen3.8-max-0902, a dated snapshot, so a probe today would measure a different serving path than this row shipped on. The 2026-09-11 Flash finding does not transfer either (different model AND different path).

The numbers here come entirely from the re-run after that was fixed, and the runner now voids any leg that produces neither a report nor a single changed file.

facts.value: One run at this tier. The effort ceiling is real but flat: the same probe shows high (9946-14061), xhigh (8266-19309) and max (6542-14902) are mutually indistinguishable with means that fall as the nominal tier rises, so max is the top of the dial and buys nothing measurable over high - the same two-rung shape the Qwen3.8-Flash probe found, which suggests it is a property of Alibaba's serving rather than of either model. Note also that this endpoint's accept-list CONTRADICTS the QwenCloud doc the superseded row relied on (low|medium|xhigh with high->xhigh), which is one more reason that row's tier claim was never safe. Cost is a list-price ESTIMATE and not a bill - DashScope exposes no credits API on this path - computed from the run's own token counts at 2.00 in / 2.50 cache-write / 0.25 cache-read / 6.00 out per MTok, from OpenRouter's Alibaba-endpoint listing. Finally, do NOT read the 9-point gain as caused by the path. It is n=1 against n=1 and almost all of it is one repo - repo 1 went 5/45 to 13/45 while repo 2 moved by one - and this board has seen the same model at the same setting swing 6 points on repo 1 (Opus 5 at medium: 11/8/14). A systematic path effect should have moved both repos and did not, so the score difference is unexplained and may simply be variance. What the pair DOES establish beyond variance is the cost and token behaviour, where the gap is ~5,000x and not a coin flip.

facts.value: The Aug 3 Qwen3.8-Max row re-run on Alibaba's OWN Anthropic-compatible endpoint - no local proxy, no aggregator - and it is the clearest demonstration on this board that a row records a SERVING PATH and not just a model. facts.value: The middle size of the Qwen3.8 family, on Alibaba's own Anthropic-compatible endpoint - the same first-party path as the Qwen3.8-Max and Qwen3.8-Flash rows, so the three sizes differ by model and by nothing else. It is the most interesting Qwen row on the board because it LOSES to both siblings and costs more than one of them: 15/105 for $6.09 against Flash's 26/105 for $1.81 and Max's 28/105 for $26.29. Eleven points below a model that costs a THIRD as much, on the same endpoint, in the same harness, on the same two repos. It is the fast one - 46.8 minutes against 97.3 and 103.4, less than half the wall clock of either sibling - so read it as a latency option and not a price/capability midpoint, because on capability per dollar there is no case for it here. *** THE EFFORT LABEL IS MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT WAS ASKED FOR *** This arm was commissioned at DEFAULT effort. On this route there is no such thing. A logging pass-through of the CLI (receipt: effort-dial-probes/20260912-claude-code-wire-default-effort.txt) shows an UNFLAGGED Claude Code putting output_config.effort=xhigh on every main call - Claude Code has no send-nothing mode - and this endpoint IMPLEMENTS that field: it 400-rejects bogus_zzz and names its accept-list (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), the same five the other two Qwen3.8 sizes expose. So an out-of-the-box run here is an xhigh run, the row says xhigh, and the arm passes --effort xhigh explicitly so the result does not depend on a CLI default that can change under it. facts.value: The first ZERO on this board. Sixty-seven rows in, the floor was 4 of 105; this is 0 of 105, and its sibling below is the other one. It is also among the cheapest rows here at twelve cents, and the two facts are the same fact: it finished both repos in under four minutes combined because it barely engaged with either. On repo 1 it made eight tool calls in 64 seconds, wrote no report, changed no file and stopped. On repo 2 it did better and it is worth saying so - 33 turns, five real edits, and a full bug report with file, symptom, root cause and patch for each entry - but it PRINTED that report into the transcript instead of writing it to the path the prompt names, so the leg was judged on its diff alone. Judged on the diff it found none of the 60 planted bugs; it did find one genuine issue nobody planted, plus one cosmetic. So the failure is not that it cannot read code. It is that it stops early, and once it stops it has produced nothing the task asked for. *** THIS IS THE THIRD ATTEMPT AT THIS ARM AND THE FIRST CLEAN ONE, WHICH THE ROW WOULD BE DISHONEST WITHOUT *** Pass 1 ran before the harness carried any context declaration. Pass 2 ran with --autocompact 100000 on it, a flag since measured INERT on both routes by two controlled pairs - so whatever pass 2 was, it was not the flag doing it. Both passes were discarded and their rows dropped before this one ran. Pass 3 carries no flag and it is mechanically clean on both legs: terminal_reason=completed, zero auto-compactions, no breaker, no truncation, no denied tool call. That matters because this board voids a leg whose ENVIRONMENT failed and scores a leg whose MODEL failed, and the runner checks the transcript to tell them apart rather than guessing from an exit code. Here it counted successful tool calls and zero permission denials on every leg. The environment was fine. *** EFFORT IS THE PROVIDER DEFAULT AND THE ROUTE IS PROBED, NOT ASSUMED *** The arm carries no --effort flag, and that is a weaker claim than it sounds: a logging pass-through measured an UNFLAGGED Claude Code putting output_config.effort=xhigh on every main call, so there is no send-nothing mode. OpenRouter does not implement output_config, so on this route the tier is dropped in transit and what runs is Groq's own default - which is what makes default honest here and would not make it honest on a first-party endpoint. Receipts: effort-dial-probes/20260912-claude-code-wire-default-effort.txt and effort-dial-probes/20260912-gptoss120b-groq-openrouter.txt. OPEN WEIGHTS ON SOMEONE ELSE'S HARDWARE: OpenAI-released weights served by Groq, pinned with allow_fallbacks=false. More than twenty hosts serve these slugs and OpenRouter load-balances per request, so an unpinned run measures a blend rather than a model. Groq is the pin because it is the one host serving BOTH sizes, so this row and its sibling differ by parameter count and by nothing else. Cost is a REAL OpenRouter credits delta, not an estimate. READ THE PAIR, NOT THE ROW: the two gpt-oss sizes bracket a question this board has otherwise answered only with money, which is whether scale alone buys bug-finding. At this end of the market it buys nothing measurable - both sizes score zero, and the larger one is the one that stopped fastest.

facts.value: GLM-5.3 Flash on Z.ai's OWN Anthropic-compatible endpoint - no aggregator, no shim, the same first-party path as the full-size GLM-5.3 row, so the two sizes differ by model and by nothing else. It scores 19 of 105 for 95 cents in 58 minutes, which is the same 19 the full-size model scores on the same endpoint at the same asserted tier, for a sixteenth of the money. *** THIS NOTE TOLD READERS NOT TO CREDIT THE EFFORT DIAL. IT IS ANSWERED, 2026-09-13, AND THE DIAL GETS THE CREDIT *** A leg at low on this exact path scores 9 of 105 against this row's 19, with route, harness, model, prompt and repos all held fixed - so THE TIER IS WORTH TEN POINTS ON THIS MODEL and the OpenRouter row's 13 sits inside the range the dial alone covers. Superseded wording, kept verbatim rather than deleted: do not read the jump from the OpenRouter Flash row as an effort result; Flash scored 13 through OpenRouter and 19 here, and the tempting story is that the tier now binds; the control on this board argues against it, because the full-size model scored 19 on BOTH routes, so the same change of route and tier moved it by zero; each of these is one run and a 6-point move on n=1 does not clear the run-to-run spread measured elsewhere. THE CONTROL ITSELF IS NOT RETRACTED: the full-size GLM-5.3 has no tier pair on this board, only a route pair, so the zero it moved is a statement about its ROUTE and says nothing about its dial, which nobody has run. What was wrong was generalising one model's route result onto another model's tier. *** EFFORT max IS A SETTING, NOT A REQUEST *** Receipt: effort-dial-probes/20260912-glm53flash-zai-anthropic.txt. The endpoint validates output_config.effort - the field Claude Code actually puts on the wire - against a CLOSED enum: low, high and max return 200 while none, minimal, medium, xhigh and an invented bogus_zzz are all rejected HTTP 400 code 1210, and a bad model id is rejected separately as 1211, so the effort rejection is about the field rather than about a malformed request. An endpoint that refuses everything outside its list is not silently clamping what is inside it. Identical accept-list on both GLM sizes. NOTE THE FIELD, because it nearly produced the opposite verdict: a first pass probed top-level reasoning_effort, which is Z.ai's own OpenAI-compatible field name, got HTTP 200 on bogus_zzz and would have published this path as inert. output_config is what the endpoint reads and what the CLI sends. max is also Z.ai's documented default for this family, so a default run and a max run here are the same run - the row asserts the tier rather than relying on that. WHY THIS ROW IS LATE: the 2026-09-10 first-party pass tried Flash first and got HTTP 429 on this key, so it was written against the full-size model and Flash kept its aggregator row. The 429 is gone. *** AND THE LABEL MOVES WITH THE EVIDENCE: first_party -> verified_ceiling *** It shipped as first_party because the accept-list proved only that the endpoint READS the field. The low leg separates the levels on this serving path - 10 points of score and 3.1x the output tokens - which is what verified requires, and the same accept-list makes max the top rung that exists, which is what promotes it to a ceiling. Honesty profile: 10 of 45 on repo 1 with ONE claimed-only, 9 of 60 plus 2 partials on repo 2 with none, and 4 genuine extras across both. billing=LIST ESTIMATE, NOT A BILL: Z.ai publishes no balance or usage endpoint on this plan key, so no credits delta exists to read; costed at the same published Flash rates the OpenRouter Flash row was billed at, which keeps the two Flash rows comparable - those rates carry a launch discount that can lapse. ctx 1M, model string [1m].

facts.value: The BOTTOM of Z.ai's three-tier dial for this family, run first-party on the same endpoint as the published max row - low, high and max are the entire accept-list here, medium does not exist and cannot be run, and max is also Z.ai's documented default, so low is a tier that has to be asked for and sits BELOW the out-of-the-box run. *** THE DIAL BINDS ON SCORE, AND THIS IS THE FIRST SINGLE-VARIABLE TIER PAIR THIS BOARD HAS RUN ON Z.AI *** 9 of 105 here against 19 at max: same endpoint, same harness, same model, one notch of one field between them. THE TIER IS WORTH TEN POINTS. It shows on the work volume too - 36,777 output tokens against the max run's 115,653, a 3.1x gap - and on the clock, 29.0 minutes against 58.4. *** AND IT ANSWERS A CAUTION THE max ROW PUBLISHED, AGAINST THAT ROW'S READING *** The max row scored 19 against the OpenRouter Flash row's 13 and said in as many words: do not read the jump as an effort result, read 19 as where Flash lands first-party rather than as what max bought. Its reason was the full-size GLM-5.3 control, which scored 19 on BOTH routes. That caution was the honest state of the evidence and the single-variable leg did not exist. It exists now and the dial moves this model by ten points, so the OpenRouter row's 13 sits INSIDE the range the tier alone covers. THE CONTROL IS NOT RETRACTED: the full-size model has no tier pair on this board, only a route pair, so the zero it moved is a statement about its ROUTE and says nothing about its dial, which nobody has run. *** WHERE IT BREAKS IS REPO 2, ALMOST ENTIRELY *** Repo 1 gives up 3 points, 7 of 45 here against 10 at max. Repo 2 nearly collapses: 2 of 60 against 9. The larger and more tangled codebase is where the missing thinking is missed, which is the same place every cheap row on this board loses its points, and it is worth more than the combined number. *** THE PRICE IS HONEST, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE OTHER DIAL PUBLISHED TODAY *** Cost per strict fix: 4.6 cents at low, 5.0 cents at max. You pay 2.2x and you get 2.1x, so the bottom rung is not a value play - it is proportionally less of everything. Compare Muse Spark 1.3 on Meta's endpoint, published hours earlier, where xhigh costs 44% more than high and buys a single point. Two dials, two entirely different value shapes, same method. Honesty profile: 7 of 45 on repo 1 with no partials and no claimed-only, 2 of 60 on repo 2 with no partials and TWO claimed-only, and 4 genuine unplanted extras. Stated flat rather than framed: that is up from one claimed-only on the max row and down from five on the OpenRouter Flash row, so it is inside this model's own range and is not evidence that the bottom rung is less honest.

facts.value: One run at each of the three tiers, so every step on this dial is n=1 against n=1. The monotonic ordering across three rungs is more than any single pair would give, but it is three single runs and a repeat at any rung could reorder the middle. THE 3-POINT GAP TO max IS NOT CLAIMED AS REAL. It is smaller than the 6-point OpenRouter gap this board declined to credit on the max row, and it should be read the same way: high and max are close enough that this pair does not separate them. What the dial DOES separate is low from the other two, by 7 and 10 points. WALL CLOCK ON THIS ROW IS NOT A CLEAN-ROOM FIGURE AND THE AUTOMATIC MARKER DID NOT CATCH IT. The repo 2 leg overlapped a Meta arm on a different provider for about 3 of its 32 minutes, before that arm was stopped. *** THIS SENTENCE GAVE THE WRONG REASON AND IS CORRECTED 2026-09-13, SAME DAY *** The runner does NOT only snapshot at the start: it samples the live-leg registry at leg start AND at leg end and unions the two, and has since cross-provider parallelism was first allowed. A leg joined later IS caught if it is still running at the end. What actually happened here is narrower: the Meta arm both ARRIVED and DEPARTED between those two samples - it joined about 3 minutes in and was force-killed before this leg finished - so it existed at neither endpoint. Two point samples cannot see an interval that fits strictly between them. Superseded wording, kept verbatim rather than deleted: the runner stamps concurrent_with= by snapshotting the live-leg registry when a leg STARTS, so a leg that is JOINED later records nothing - this one started first and carries no marker. Three minutes of a mostly-installing neighbour is a negligible effect on a 62-minute total and it can only inflate, never shrink, but the row says it rather than implying a measurement it did not make. CLOSED 2026-09-13, after the wave: the runner now samples the peer registry on every tick of the 30-second keep-alive sweep it already runs, and the row carries the union across all samples - so a peer that lives longer than one tick can no longer slip between the endpoints. Verified against a transient peer that is invisible to both. billing=LIST ESTIMATE, NOT A BILL: Z.ai publishes no balance or usage endpoint on this plan key, so no credits delta exists to read; costed at the same published Flash rates the other three Flash rows were costed at, which keeps them comparable - and those rates carry a launch discount that can lapse. This endpoint does not report reasoning tokens separately, so output volume is the only work proxy available across the dial. ctx 1M.

facts.value: The MIDDLE rung of Z.ai's three-tier dial, and the row that completes it. low, high and max are the entire accept-list for this family - none, minimal, medium, xhigh and an invented value are all refused HTTP 400 code 1210 - so EVERY TIER THIS ENDPOINT WILL SERVE FOR THIS MODEL NOW HAS A BENCH ROW, which no other model on this board can say. *** THE DIAL IS MONOTONIC ON SCORE *** 9 at low, 16 here, 19 at max, with output volume rising alongside it - 36,777 then 97,332 then 115,653 tokens. This is a dial that works, measured end to end on one serving path with the route, the harness, the model, the prompt and the repos all held fixed. *** AND IT IS NOT MONOTONIC ON VALUE, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF *** Cost per strict fix runs 4.6 cents at low, 5.9 cents HERE, and 5.0 cents at max. THE MIDDLE RUNG IS THE WORST BUY ON THE DIAL. Muse Spark 1.3 did the same thing hours earlier on Meta's stack, where xhigh cost 78 cents per fix against 57 at high and 60 at max. Two vendors, two unrelated dials, two different harnesses, same shape - the middle is where the money goes and the score does not follow. That is not something a tier name or a token sweep would tell you. *** ON THIS STACK high IS DOMINATED BY max, ON ALL THREE COLUMNS AT ONCE *** high costs 0.94 dollars against max's 0.95, takes LONGER in wall clock - 62.3 minutes against 58.3 - and scores three fewer. There is no reading of those numbers on which a buyer should pick high here, which is worth saying plainly because the tier name suggests otherwise. *** IT ALSO LOCATES THE OPENROUTER FLASH ROW, WITHOUT SETTLING IT *** That row scores 13 with 70,628 output tokens. Both figures sit BETWEEN low and high on this dial, not at the top of it - so whatever OpenRouter serves for this model, it is demonstrably not the ceiling, even though Z.ai documents max as this family's default. What tier it IS serving remains unknown: that route ignores the effort field this board sends, which is what inert_default records, and nothing here identifies what it substitutes. Honesty profile: 9 of 45 on repo 1 and 7 of 60 on repo 2, no partials on either, ONE claimed-only per repo, and 4 genuine unplanted extras. Two claimed-only sits between the max row's one and the OpenRouter row's five, so the claim record does not track the tier.

facts.value: The FIRST configuration outside Meta's effort dial to be run three times, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 27, 30 and 29 of 105 (repo 1: 8, 14, 13 - repo 2: 19, 16, 16). Mean 28.7, range 3. *** WHAT THIS CORRECTS IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A NUMBER *** The single run this replaces scored 27, and its note read that as settled because the 2026-08-12 concurrent-legs run had also scored 27 - 'n=2 agreement'. Two further sequential runs came in at 30 and 29. The 27 was correct for the run that produced it; what does not survive is treating a pair of agreeing draws as a measurement of the rung. Both 27s sit at the bottom of the range this configuration actually spans. *** WHERE THE MOVEMENT IS, AND WHAT THAT IS WORTH *** The three totals span 3 points, but the per-repo legs span more: repo 1 scored 8, 14 and 13 of 45, repo 2 scored 19, 16 and 16 of 60. The repo-1 range alone is 6 points on a 45-bug repo, wider than the range of the totals it feeds. The legs moved in opposite directions and the totals landed close together. That is an OBSERVATION about three runs and nothing more - it is not a mechanism, and it is not a claim that totals are steadier than legs. Three draws cannot establish that, and this pattern arises from chance often enough to be unremarkable. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0. Per-leg (repo 1 / repo 2): wall 19.1/22.0, 18.8/23.5 and 23.9/21.9 minutes; floor 6.84/10.12, 9.38/8.59 and 13.57/7.30 dollars. Genuine extras 16, 16 and 22. Claimed-only 1, 0 and 1, all on repo 1. COST IS A FLOOR, NOT A BILL: the grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row on this board is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates. The three floors are 16.96, 17.96 and 20.88 dollars and this row shows their mean. That spread is not pricing noise - the reconstruction scales with how many inference requests a run made (106, 118 and 128 across the three), so it tracks real differences in how much work the agent did. SEQUENTIAL legs throughout - one repo at a time, one machine, one key - which is what 'seq' means in the name and why this wall is comparable to the rest of the board. Effort verified active by a fresh zero-token ACP readback before each launch. Judge: Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs.

facts.value: THE TOP ROW OF THIS BOARD, RUN THREE TIMES. Runs scored 48, 40 and 47 of 105 (repo 1: 24, 21, 21 - repo 2: 24, 19, 26). Mean 45.0, range 8. *** WHY THIS ARM MATTERED MOST *** Every other row is read against the leader, so the leader was the single run whose spread was worth the most and known the least. It is still the leader: 45.0 is the highest figure on the board and no other row is close to it at n=3. What changed is the width. *** THE RANGE IS 8 POINTS, AND IT IS NOT A SMALL NUMBER HERE *** Eight points of 105 is wider than the gap between the leader and the row below it, wider than most adjacent pairs anywhere on this board, and it sits on a configuration nothing about which was varied: same model, prompt, harness, route, effort flag and judge. The single run published on 2026-09-04 scored 48, which is the TOP of its own three-run range, so every comparison drawn against 48 was drawn against this configuration's best day rather than its typical one. That is not a correction to the old row - 48 happened, and its receipt stands - it is a correction to what the number could be used for. *** WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT MOVE *** It does not change the ORDER at the top: 45.0 still leads, and the gap to the next row is now 2 points rather than 5. It does mean that gap is inside the leader's own measured spread, so 'Astra max beats the row below it' is no longer something this board can assert - the row below is itself a single run with an unmeasured spread. Two numbers of unknown width two points apart support no ordering at all. *** THE UNPLANTED COLUMN MOVED FAR MORE THAN THE SCORE *** Genuine extras came in at 45, 58 and 62 across the three runs, a range of 17 on a count that is not scored. The score varied by 8 while the unscored work varied by 17, which is worth knowing before anyone reads a single run's extras figure as a property of a model. All six legs were clean: every leg exited 0, none carries a handicap note, and zero claimed-only fixes were recorded across all six - this arm claimed nothing the judge did not confirm, on any run. Per-leg receipts (repo 1 / repo 2): wall 37.2/41.6, 51.3/44.7 and 35.9/58.7 minutes; cost 15.07/16.14, 17.59/16.14 and 12.33/21.82 dollars. Run 3 ran 20 per cent longer than run 1 and scored one point lower. *** ONE JUDGING NOTE, BECAUSE IT NEARLY BECAME A SILENT DIFFERENCE *** Run 3's repo-2 leg created a scratch directory for itself, holding 300 copies of the files it was about to edit. Every copy was verified byte-identical to the pristine repo, so it contained no fix and no evidence, but left in the diff it would have added two megabytes to that leg's judge packet - a packet neither of the other two runs had. It is excluded, so all three runs were judged on the same shape of evidence. The alternative repair, raising the size limit, would have judged one replicate on a materially different packet from its own siblings. facts.value: DeepSeek's top Flash rung, RUN THREE TIMES. Runs scored 24, 19 and 22 of 105 (repo 1: 14, 10, 10 - repo 2: 10, 9, 12). Mean 21.7, range 5. *** THE ONE ARM IN THIS WAVE WHOSE REPLICATION IS VERIFIED *** Three flash arms were replicated on the same nights; this is the only one where the harness left enough behind to check that the three runs ran in the same configuration. All six legs resolved deepseek-flash with the 1M window, and NONE of them compacted: peak live context 513,330 / 509,936 / 471,821 on repo 1 and 520,206 / 544,170 / 558,074 on repo 2, against a harness that would have thrown context away at about 30 per cent had it been triggered. A mean is a claim that its members differ only by chance, and on this row that claim was tested rather than assumed. *** ONE THING WAS NOT HELD FIXED *** The 2026-09-10 run ran Claude Code 2.1.267 and both replicates ran 2.1.270. The CLI self-updates between waves. It is stated rather than buried because the resolved model and the compaction behaviour are identical across all six legs, so the version string is the only difference the receipts show. *** WHAT THE SPREAD LOOKS LIKE *** The totals span 5 points, and the two repos moved in OPPOSITE directions: repo 1 fell 14, 10, 10 while repo 2 rose 10, 9, 12. That is an observation about three runs, not a mechanism, and it is not a claim that totals are steadier than legs - three draws cannot establish that. The published single run scored 24, the TOP of its own three-run range, so every comparison drawn against 24 was drawn against this configuration's best day. *** THE WALL COLUMN ON THIS ROW IS NOISY AND THE PER-LEG FIGURES ARE THE HONEST FORM *** Against the control's tokens per minute the four replicate legs ran 47, 131, 118 and 104 per cent - in both directions, same binary, same night. The 47 per cent leg is the one that overlapped hardest with two other arms running concurrently. Do not read a ratio off this row. *** EVER VS ALWAYS - THE THING A SINGLE RUN CANNOT SHOW *** Across the three runs this arm ever fixed 33 distinct bugs of 105, well above the 21.7 any single run manages. Of those 33, only 11 fell in ALL THREE runs; 10 fell in two and 12 in exactly one. A third of what it ever fixed is what it reliably fixes. It is the LEAST consistent of the three flash arms replicated in this wave despite scoring the highest of them, which is exactly the trade a single number hides. The Coverage view shades each tick by its observed hit rate, so this is readable on the row. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0. Per-leg (repo 1 / repo 2): wall 25.4/17.2, 59.9/18.1 and 20.6/26.4 minutes; bill 0.62/0.46, 0.30/0.29 and 0.31/0.36 dollars. Genuine extras 7, 6 and 7. Each leg is a full independent run of both repos; the mean is over three, and the per-repo runs are stated so the spread stays visible - it is the finding, not a caveat on it. billing=REAL bill: the runner snapshots the DeepSeek balance before and after each leg and writes the drop, so this cost column is money that moved, not a list estimate. Judge: Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs.

facts.value: GLM-5.3 Flash's top rung on Z.ai's own endpoint, RUN THREE TIMES. Runs scored 19, 18 and 16 of 105 (repo 1: 10, 9, 9 - repo 2: 9, 9, 7). Mean 17.7, range 3 - the TIGHTEST spread of the three flash arms replicated in this wave. *** THE REPLICATION IS UNVERIFIED, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE ROUTE *** This board now checks, before publishing a mean, that its members ran in the same harness configuration. On this arm that check CANNOT RUN. Z.ai's Anthropic-compatible endpoint reports input_tokens: 0 on every turn and emits no compaction records, so peak context and compaction count are BLANK, not zero. What is readable: all three runs resolved glm-5.3-flash with the 1M window, and the CLI went 2.1.269 for the first run to 2.1.270 for the other two. Beyond that there is nothing to compare. Read this row as three runs that are believed to match and were not confirmed to - which is a weaker statement than the DeepSeek Flash row on this same board can make, and the difference is worth seeing. *** WHAT THE SPREAD SUPPORTS *** A fixed configuration produced 19, 18 and 16. The published single run scored 19, the TOP of that range. facts.value: Google's newest Flash on its own agent CLI, RUN THREE TIMES. Runs scored 20, 19 and 15 of 105 (repo 1: 7, 7, 6 - repo 2: 13, 12, 9). Mean 18.0, range 5. *** THE REPLICATION IS UNVERIFIED, AND THIS HARNESS IS THE BLINDEST ON THE BOARD *** The Antigravity CLI writes no session init record at all, so nothing about context size, compaction or even its own version is recoverable from the transcripts. Where the Z.ai rows are missing token counts, this one is missing the record that would carry them. So it is not known whether the three runs met the same conditions, and it is not known what harness version the 2026-09-02 control ran against the 2026-09-15 replicates. Stated plainly rather than left to be inferred from an absence. *** THE WALL COLUMN IS SLOWER THAN ITS CONTROL AND NOBODY KNOWS WHY *** All four replicate legs ran at 68, 71, 74 and 83 per cent of the 2026-09-02 control's tokens per minute - 17 to 32 per cent slower, every leg, in one direction. TWO EXPLANATIONS WERE CHECKED AND BOTH FAILED. Box contention: the GLM arm ran under the identical three-lane load at 100 and 143 per cent of its own control, so a busy machine does not explain it. Provider throttling: one leg did die on a hard Google quota wall (Individual quota reached, resets in 3h34m11s) and was re-run, and the throttling story predicted that the re-run - alone on an idle box with a freshly reset quota, the cleanest conditions any leg in this wave got - would come back near the control's rate. It came back the SLOWEST OF THE FOUR. A hypothesis that predicts fast and gets the slowest run of the set under its own best conditions is refuted, not refined. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and no cause is asserted on this row. What it does not touch: the scores. Every score on this board is judged from the diff against a withheld answer key, so wall and cost are the only columns a slow leg can move. *** WHAT THE SCORES SHOW *** The published single run scored 20, the TOP of the three. Repo 2 carries almost all of this arm's score and all of its movement (13, 12, 9 against repo 1's 7, 7, 6), and repo 1 produced ZERO genuine unplanted extras on all three runs. *** EVER VS ALWAYS *** Across the three runs this arm ever fixed 24 distinct bugs of 105 against a mean of 18.0, and 14 of those 24 fell in ALL THREE runs - 2 in two, 8 in exactly one. It fixes the FEWEST distinct bugs of the three flash arms replicated in this wave and repeats the largest share of them. Counts over three runs, not a measured reliability. *** RECEIPTS *** All six scored legs exited 0; the quota-killed leg scored nothing and is not in this mean. Per-leg (repo 1 / repo 2): wall 13.2/16.6, 20.7/22.9 and 18.6/24.2 minutes; cost 5.0131/4.7741, 6.4788/5.3301 and 5.9592/5.5222 dollars. Genuine extras 6, 2 and 4. Claimed-only 1, 0 and 0 across six legs. Each leg is a full independent run of both repos; the mean is over three, and the per-repo runs are stated so the spread stays visible. high is the TOP tier this CLI offers for 3.8 Flash - agy models lists only low, medium and high, and --effort max is rejected outright, so it cannot silently clamp. billing=LIST ESTIMATE, NOT A BILL: Google list rates through 2026-12-31. Judge: Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs.

facts.value: THE MIDDLE SIZE OF THE QWEN3.8 FAMILY, RUN THREE TIMES ON ALIBABA'S OWN FIRST-PARTY ENDPOINT. Runs scored 15, 13 and 17 of 105 (repo 1: 6, 5, 6 - repo 2: 9, 8, 11). Mean 15.0, range 4. *** THE FINDING FROM THE SINGLE RUN SURVIVES AT n=3 *** The n=1 row (15/105) was the most interesting Qwen row on the board because it LOST to both siblings and cost more than one of them. The mean does not soften that: at 15.0 it is still eleven points below Qwen3.8-Flash's 26/105 and well below Qwen3.8-Max's 28/105, on the same endpoint, the same harness and the same two repos. It is still the fast one - a combined wall mean of 56.8 minutes against Flash's 97.3 and Max's 103.4 - so read it as a latency option rather than a price/capability midpoint; on capability per dollar there is still no case for it here. *** THE EFFORT LABEL IS MEASURED, NOT REQUESTED, AND THAT DOES NOT CHANGE WITH REPLICATION *** This arm is commissioned at DEFAULT effort. On this route there is no such thing: a logging pass-through of the CLI (receipt: effort-dial-probes/20260912-claude-code-wire-default-effort.txt) shows an unflagged Claude Code putting output_config.effort=xhigh on every main call, and the endpoint validates and echoes that field. The dial itself was probed once, not three times - it is a property of the endpoint's wire protocol, not of an individual run, so it does not need re-verifying per leg. Honesty profile across the three runs, mean per repo: repo 1 fixed 5.7/45 with zero partials, repo 2 fixed 9.3/60 with 0.7 partials; claimed-only 2.0 and 2.3; genuine unplanted extras 0.7 and 1.7; false-positive fixes zero on both, all three runs. Per-leg receipts (repo 1 / repo 2): wall 24.8/22.0, 24.5/43.4 and 26.8/28.8 minutes; cost 2.48/3.61, 1.63/3.60 and 2.11/3.23 dollars. All six legs were clean - every leg exited 0, none carries a handicap note. ONE WALL FIGURE IS FLAGGED, NOT EXPLAINED: two of the three repo-2 legs shared the machine with another running leg, and this board's own metrics record that as contention rather than silently folding it into the mean. Contention can inflate a wall figure, never shrink it, and it does not touch score, tokens or cost. facts.value: ONE RUN, against a control that has three. The first-party row is a mean of 15, 13 and 17; this is a single 8 with no measured spread of its own, so the gap between them is known far less precisely than two numbers side by side suggest. billing=REAL BILL, and the control's is NOT: this figure is a credits delta read from OpenRouter before and after each leg, while the first-party row is a token-count estimate at list rates, because that endpoint publishes no usage API. A bill and an estimate are not the same kind of number and the 2.11-against-5.55 comparison should be read with that in mind. Token counts are NOT quoted for this row at all: for an arm behind a shim the local CLI invents them from an Anthropic price table, so they describe nothing real. EFFORT IS NOT ASSERTED. The first-party sibling runs at a MEASURED xhigh - that endpoint implements the effort field and rejects invalid values. OpenRouter does not implement it, so no tier was requested and none is claimed; the model reasons on its own regardless. THE CONTEXT DECLARATION OVERSTATES THE HOST, DELIBERATELY AND VISIBLY: the arm declares a 1M window to the CLI because through a shim that is the ONLY override the CLI accepts - every numeric alternative is passed through verbatim and rejected upstream as an unknown model id. This host's real ceiling is 262,144. The declaration never reaches the wire and only sets the CLI's local compaction arithmetic; the run peaked at about 203K, some 59K under the real ceiling. The earlier configuration, which accepted the CLI's 200K fallback instead, compacted 43 times on repo 1 and was killed outright on repo 2 - that attempt is void and is not this row.

facts.value: The same Qwen3.8-27B weights as the first-party row, served at fp8 by a THIRD-PARTY host and reached through an aggregator - OpenRouter, pinned to one provider with fallbacks off, because OpenRouter lists 16 hosts for this slug at three different precisions (10 fp8, one bf16, one fp4) and an unpinned run blends across them per request and measures nothing. 8 of 105, against 15.0 for the first-party n=3 mean of the same model. That is below the WHOLE measured range of the control, whose three runs scored 15, 13 and 17. *** DO NOT READ THIS AS THE PRICE OF fp8 QUANTIZATION *** Two things changed together and this pair isolates neither: the PRECISION went from native to fp8, and the ROUTE went from Alibaba's own endpoint to an aggregator plus a third-party host. The same trap the Muse Spark OpenRouter-vs-first-party pair hit. A run that would separate them - this host at native precision, or Alibaba's endpoint at fp8 - does not exist and cannot be bought here, because neither party serves the other half. *** AND THE TWO ROWS DID NOT RUN IN THE SAME CONTEXT REGIME *** This is the more specific reason the gap is not clean. Through a shim the CLI cannot learn the upstream window, so this arm compacted 3 times on repo 1 and 2 times on repo 2; the first-party control compacted ZERO times on either repo and peaked at about 27K. Compaction throws context away mid-run, so part of this gap is a harness difference rather than a model difference. It is stated rather than corrected because nothing here can separate the two. WHAT IT IS GOOD AT: it is CHEAPER and no slower - 2.11 dollars against the control's 5.55, and 59.0 minutes against 56.8. And it did not over-claim: ZERO claimed-only fixes on either repo, so every fix it reported, the blind judge confirmed. It found 2 unplanted defects nobody had seeded, one per repo.

facts.value: THE FIRST REPLICATION OF THIS MODEL'S TOP EFFORT SETTING. Runs scored 40 and 47 of 105 (repo 1: 18, 20 - repo 2: 22, 27). Mean 43.5, range 7. *** WHY THIS ROW IS n=2 AND NOT n=3 *** A third run was attempted on 2026-09-16 and did not complete: it ran 156 minutes, finished 563 tool calls, and then the harness account's usage quota was exhausted mid-turn. It produced no report and recorded no tokens and no cost, so there is nothing to score and nothing to average. It is not on this board and is not counted as a low run - a leg that never finished is not a result. Re-running it was declined on cost. *** THE SINGLE-RUN ROW ABOVE SAYS 42 AND THIS MEAN USES 40 FOR THE SAME RUN. BOTH ARE REAL. *** Run 1's transcript has been judged twice. The 2026-07-31 pass scored 19 + 23 = 42 and recorded its judge as grok-4.5 with no served-model field at all, because that column did not exist yet. The 2026-09-13 re-judge scored 18 + 22 = 40 and recorded the model the server actually served, grok-4.6. The judge bridge's model flag is inert - a measurement from 2026-09-04, where grok-4.5, grok-4.6 and a deliberately nonexistent model string all came back as grok-4.6 - so the July pass recorded a REQUEST as though it were a fact and was in all likelihood served the same judge. This mean therefore uses 40: the pass whose judge identity was MEASURED, and the same pass configuration run 2 was scored under. That makes it comparable and documented, NOT more accurate, and the older row keeps its 42 as a receipt rather than being quietly rewritten. *** WHAT THE TWO PASSES BUY, WHICH IS AN ERROR BAR AND NOT SAMPLE SIZE *** They disagree on 3 bugs of 105: on repo 1 one bug moved from a full fix to a partial, on repo 2 two credited bugs became misses. So JUDGE variance on a fixed transcript is 2 points, against MODEL variance of 7 points between the two runs - run-to-run spread is roughly three and a half times the grading noise. Two gradings of one transcript are NOT two runs and were not treated as such; n counts runs of the model. *** THE TWO RUNS COST VERY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS FOR A 7-POINT GAIN *** Run 2 consumed 74 percent more tokens than run 1 (100.9M against 176.0M) and 74 percent more at list rates (69.61 against 121.09 dollars) to score 7 points higher. The runs are six weeks apart on a self-updating CLI that records no version in its transcripts, so whether that is the same model working harder or a changed serving path is NOT established here. Read the mean as a mean of two runs that differed in effort expended as well as in outcome. *** THE REGIME BEHIND THESE TWO RUNS IS UNVERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED *** The automated regime check reads context accounting out of transcripts; this harness reports none - no init record and zero input tokens on every turn - so it returns CANNOT TELL for both repos rather than confirming the runs match. Stated plainly because the alternative is implying a check that did not happen. *** WALL TIME IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS THE TWO RUNS *** Run 1's legs ran alone; both of run 2's legs shared the machine with other work and say so in their own rows. Contention can inflate a wall figure and cannot shrink it, so the wall mean here is an upper bound. Scores, tokens and cost are unaffected by it. *** WHAT IS SOLID *** Counts, not inferences. A fixed configuration produced 40 and 47 of 105. Run 2 needed five attempts to produce two clean legs - three earlier legs died on wall budgets or non-zero exits and one was orphaned - so the failure rate of this configuration on this hardware is itself part of the picture and is visible in the metrics receipts.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at xhigh through xAI's own CLI, the first 4.7 row on this board, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 25, 30 and 31 of 105 (repo 1: 12, 12, 16 - repo 2: 13, 18, 15). Mean 28.7, range 6. *** THE HEADLINE IS THAT NOTHING MOVED *** Grok 4.6 at the SAME tier, also a mean of three, stands at 28.7 of 105. This row is 28.7. Three runs a side at a verified ceiling, and the totals are identical to the decimal - the cleanest null result this board has produced for a generation step. It is published as one. A tie is a measurement, and publishing only when a number improves would make this a scoreboard for vendors rather than a benchmark. *** THE IDENTICAL TOTAL HIDES A SWAP *** Repo 1 scored 12, 12, 16 of 45 against 4.6's mean of 11.7; repo 2 scored 13, 18, 15 of 60 against 17.0. Up about a point and a half on one codebase, down about the same on the other. Both movements sit inside the spread of the runs that produced them, so this is a direction worth testing and not a finding. *** WHAT DOES MOVE, AND IT MOVES THE WRONG WAY: COST *** Reconstructed floors of $16.54, $23.04, $29.94 for a mean of $23.17, against $16.89 for the three 4.6 runs on the SAME arithmetic - about 37% more for the same score. READ THE COST COLUMN CAREFULLY: the reconstruction used to take the largest context in a run and charge every request in that run against it, which overstates any run that fans out into subagents by up to 25%, and it now measures each session separately. This row carries the corrected figure. The 4.6 row still shows $18.60 on the old arithmetic and has not yet been restated; on that same old arithmetic these three runs come to $26.18. So the gap is about a third either way. What is inconsistent across the board right now is the arithmetic, not the finding. Both numbers are floors twice over: the grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates - the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis, and xAI prices 4.7 identically to 4.6 - and xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates, which these runs did, by an amount this method cannot see. *** AND WHAT MOVES IN 4.7'S FAVOUR: BUGS NOBODY PLANTED *** Genuine extras - real defects found in the repo that are not part of the planted set - ran 26, 35, 34 across the three runs, a mean of 31.7, against 18.0 for 4.6: roughly 76% more. The most defensible reading of this wave is that 4.7 finds materially more real bugs than 4.6 and no more of the ones being counted. Whether that is a better bug-hunter or a worse instruction-follower is a judgment the number does not settle. *** PER BUG, THE TWO MODELS ARE NEARLY THE SAME MODEL *** Across three runs a side, on repo 1 each touched 18 distinct planted bugs with 15 shared; on repo 2 it was 21 against 22 with 18 shared. There is not one bug on either repo that 4.6 found on all three runs and 4.7 never found - zero hard regressions - and exactly one that 4.7 found on all three and 4.6 never did. Every other bug unique to one model was a single-run hit: noise, not capability. Consistency shifted in opposite directions per repo: 4.7 holds 10 bugs on all three runs against 4.6's 5 on repo 1, and 10 against 14 on repo 2. *** THE RUNS DID NOT BEHAVE ALIKE, AND THE AUTOMATIC CHECK CANNOT SEE IT HERE *** The regime check that refuses a mean over mismatched configurations parses Claude Code transcripts, so it returns NOT CHECKED for every grok row on this board. The CLI's own session logs show what it would have looked for. Sessions spawned per leg (repo 1 / repo 2) - this model: run 1 1 and 1; run 2 1 and 3; run 3 5 and 1. The 4.6 rows at the same tier: run 1 3 and 3; run 2 4 and 3; run 3 5 and 3. 4.6 never once ran a leg as a single session; this model did it four times out of six, and when it does fan out it commits far harder - 184 and 206 inference requests against 4.6's 88 to 128. Fan-out tracks COST almost perfectly across these runs and tracks SCORE not at all: 4.6's weakest repo-1 leg fanned out to three sessions, and the two single-session repo-1 legs here scored the same as each other. The arm definitions are byte-identical clones, so this is emergent agent behaviour rather than configuration - the same class of hidden difference the regime check was built for. An OBSERVATION over three runs, not a mechanism. *** THE TIER IS THE MODEL CEILING AND THAT WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED *** A zero-token ACP readback before each launch returned reasoning_effort xhigh for a requested xhigh, and the enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh with high as the CLI default - nothing above xhigh exists to ask for. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string, so an echo is the only thing that makes this label honest. The served model is named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0. Per-run wall 39.6, 47.3, 51.8 minutes against 43.1 for the 4.6 mean - but that comparison is NOT decidable from this wave: only run 1 had the machine to itself, runs 2 and 3 overlapped each other, and contention biases a wall upward. On the one uncontended run this was the fastest run at this tier the board has recorded. Legs SEQUENTIAL within every run, one repo at a time - that is what seq means here. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at xhigh through xAI's own CLI, published as the MEAN OF FOUR INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 25, 30, 31 and 29 of 105 (repo 1: 12, 12, 16, 12 - repo 2: 13, 18, 15, 17). Mean 28.8, range 6. *** THE HEADLINE IS STILL THAT NOTHING MOVED *** Grok 4.6 at the SAME tier, a mean of three, stands at 28.7 of 105. This row is 28.8. The fourth run was added specifically to test whether the tie was an artefact of three draws; it was not - the headline moved by +0.1 of a bug. This supersedes the mean-of-3 row published earlier the same day, which said the same thing on less evidence. A tie is a measurement, and publishing only when a number improves would make this a scoreboard for vendors rather than a benchmark. *** THE IDENTICAL TOTAL HIDES A SWAP, AND ONE REPO IS NEARLY CONSTANT *** Repo 1 scored 12, 12, 16, 12 of 45 against 4.6's mean of 11.7; repo 2 scored 13, 18, 15, 17 of 60 against 17.0. Three of the four repo-1 runs landed on the same number, which makes the fourth look like the outlier rather than the ceiling; repo 2 scatters across five points. Both movements sit inside the spread of the runs producing them. *** THE SPEED QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO *** Runs 2 and 3 overlapped each other on one machine, so their walls are biased upward and the earlier row published this comparison as undecidable. Runs 1 and 4 each had the machine to themselves: 39.6 and 45.4 minutes, a mean of 42.5 against 43.1 for the three 4.6 runs. That is a difference of under two minutes on runs that take three quarters of an hour. Any earlier reading that this generation is faster came from a single run and does not survive a second clean one. *** WHAT DOES MOVE, AND IT MOVES THE WRONG WAY: COST *** Reconstructed floors of $16.54, $23.04, $29.94, $22.01 for a mean of $22.88, against $16.89 for the three 4.6 runs on the SAME arithmetic - about 35% more for the same score. READ THE COST COLUMN CAREFULLY: the reconstruction used to take the largest context in a run and charge every request in that run against it, which overstates any run that fans out into subagents by up to 25%, and it now measures each session separately. This row carries the corrected figure; the 4.6 row still shows $18.60 on the old arithmetic and has not yet been restated. On that same old arithmetic these four runs come to $27.10. The gap is about a third either way - what is inconsistent across the board right now is the arithmetic, not the finding. Both are floors twice over: the grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates on the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis, and xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates, which these runs did, by an amount this method cannot see. *** AND WHAT MOVES IN 4.7'S FAVOUR: BUGS NOBODY PLANTED *** Genuine extras - real defects in the repo that are not part of the planted set - ran 26, 35, 34 and 32 across the four runs, a mean of 31.8, against 18.0 for 4.6: roughly 76% more, and the most stable difference between the two models in this whole wave. The most defensible reading is that 4.7 finds materially more real bugs than 4.6 and no more of the ones being counted. Whether that is a better bug-hunter or a worse instruction-follower is a judgment the number does not settle. *** PER BUG, THE TWO MODELS ARE NEARLY THE SAME MODEL *** Measured across the first three runs a side: on repo 1 each touched 18 distinct planted bugs with 15 shared; on repo 2, 21 against 22 with 18 shared. There is not one bug on either repo that 4.6 found on all three runs and 4.7 never found, and exactly one the other way. Every other bug unique to one model was a single-run hit - noise, not capability. *** THE RUNS DID NOT BEHAVE ALIKE, AND THE AUTOMATIC CHECK CANNOT SEE IT HERE *** The regime check that refuses a mean over mismatched configurations parses Claude Code transcripts, so it returns NOT CHECKED for every grok row on this board. The CLI's own session dirs show what it would look for: sessions spawned per leg (repo 1 / repo 2) ran run 1 1 and 1; run 2 1 and 3; run 3 5 and 1; run 4 2 and 5. Grok 4.6 never once ran a leg as a single session across its six; this model did it four times out of eight, and when it does fan out it commits far harder - up to 206 inference requests against 4.6's 88 to 128. Across these four runs fan-out tracks COST almost mechanically, and what it does to SCORE is unresolved rather than nothing: ordered by inference requests the four runs scored 25, 30, 29 and 31, so the heaviest fan-out landed mid-pack but the run with NO fan-out landed LAST, not mid-pack. The rank correlation against score is positive and four runs cannot separate that from chance. CORRECTED 2026-09-21: an earlier version of this note said the no-fan-out run landed mid-pack and that fan-out tracked score not at all; the first half was simply wrong - that run scored lowest of the four - and the second was stated more firmly than four runs support. The arm definitions are byte-identical clones, so this is emergent agent behaviour rather than configuration. An OBSERVATION over four runs, not a mechanism. *** THE TIER IS THE MODEL CEILING AND THAT WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED *** A zero-token ACP readback before each launch returned reasoning_effort xhigh for a requested xhigh, and the enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh with high as the CLI default - nothing above xhigh exists to ask for. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string, so an echo is the only thing that makes this label honest. The served model is named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. *** RECEIPTS *** All eight legs exited 0. Per-run wall 39.6, 47.3, 51.8, 45.4 minutes; runs 1 and 4 uncontended, runs 2 and 3 overlapping each other. Legs SEQUENTIAL within every run, one repo at a time - that is what seq means here. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 on all eight legs, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at high through xAI's own CLI - the CLI DEFAULT rung - what someone gets who never touches the effort setting, and the only number on this dial that describes the out-of-the-box experience. 19 of 105: 9 of 45 on repo 1 and 10 of 60 on repo 2, 18 genuine extras, 40.5 minutes, a reconstructed floor of $11.53. ONE RUN. *** AGAINST THE PREVIOUS GENERATION AT THE SAME RUNG *** Grok 4.6 (high) scored 23.0 of 105 (7 on repo 1, 16 on repo 2), also a single run, for a difference of -4. Both sides are n=1, so this is one draw against one draw. The scale of the doubt is not a guess: three runs of the 4.6 configuration one rung up spanned 27 to 30 of 105, and three runs of this model at that rung spanned 25 to 31 - so a gap of a few points between two single runs is inside what the same configuration produces run to run. *** WHERE IT SITS ON ITS OWN DIAL *** This model at xhigh is 28.8 of 105, published as a mean of four. This rung is 19, a single run. The 4.6 dial for comparison ran low 15, medium 23, high 23, xhigh 28.7 - FLAT between medium and high, which is the most interesting thing on it, and the low rung is where that dial had real room. Whether either shape repeats here is a question the rungs answer together: read this row beside its siblings rather than on its own. *** THE TIER WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND FOR THE LOWER RUNGS THAT MATTERS MORE *** A zero-token ACP readback before launch returned reasoning_effort high for a requested high. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string AND its default is `high`, so a rung that failed to apply would look identical to one that worked in every artefact except this readback - the run would simply be a default-effort run wearing another label. The enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh. The served model is named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. *** COST IS A FLOOR *** The grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates, the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis. This row uses the per-session arithmetic corrected on 2026-09-21; on the older run-level arithmetic the other grok rows still use it would read $11.54. It is a floor twice over: xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates. *** RECEIPTS *** Both legs exited 0. Legs SEQUENTIAL, one repo at a time, uncontended - nothing else ran alongside. The agent spawned 1 session(s) on repo 1 and 1 on repo 2 (57 and 73 inference requests); that count varies run to run on identical arm definitions for this model, and it tracks cost far more closely than score. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at medium through xAI's own CLI - the MEDIUM rung, one step below the CLI default. 30 of 105: 11 of 45 on repo 1 and 19 of 60 on repo 2, 30 genuine extras, 32.4 minutes, a reconstructed floor of $25.15. ONE RUN. *** AGAINST THE PREVIOUS GENERATION AT THE SAME RUNG *** Grok 4.6 (medium) scored 23.0 of 105 (7 on repo 1, 16 on repo 2), also a single run, for a difference of +7. Both sides are n=1, so this is one draw against one draw. The scale of the doubt is not a guess: three runs of the 4.6 configuration one rung up spanned 27 to 30 of 105, and three runs of this model at that rung spanned 25 to 31 - so a gap of a few points between two single runs is inside what the same configuration produces run to run. *** WHERE IT SITS ON ITS OWN DIAL *** This model at xhigh is 28.8 of 105, published as a mean of four. This rung is 30, a single run. The 4.6 dial for comparison ran low 15, medium 23, high 23, xhigh 28.7 - FLAT between medium and high, which is the most interesting thing on it, and the low rung is where that dial had real room. Whether either shape repeats here is a question the rungs answer together: read this row beside its siblings rather than on its own. *** THE TIER WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND FOR THE LOWER RUNGS THAT MATTERS MORE *** A zero-token ACP readback before launch returned reasoning_effort medium for a requested medium. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string AND its default is `high`, so a rung that failed to apply would look identical to one that worked in every artefact except this readback - the run would simply be a default-effort run wearing another label. The enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh. The served model is named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. *** COST IS A FLOOR *** The grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates, the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis. This row uses the per-session arithmetic corrected on 2026-09-21; on the older run-level arithmetic the other grok rows still use it would read $28.86. It is a floor twice over: xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates. *** RECEIPTS *** Both legs exited 0. Legs SEQUENTIAL, one repo at a time, uncontended - nothing else ran alongside. The agent spawned 3 session(s) on repo 1 and 5 on repo 2 (133 and 199 inference requests); that count varies run to run on identical arm definitions for this model, and it tracks cost far more closely than score. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at high through xAI's own CLI, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 19, 22 and 17 of 105 (repo 1: 9, 9, 8 of 45 - repo 2: 10, 13, 9 of 60).
