This supersedes the single-run row published earlier the same day at 19 of 105, which said the same thing on one draw. *** AGAINST THE PREVIOUS GENERATION AT THE SAME RUNG *** Grok 4.6 at high scored 23 of 105 (7 on repo 1, 16 on repo 2) - A SINGLE RUN, so the samples are not the same size and the comparison is three draws against one. Difference -3.7. That 4.6 number falls OUTSIDE the spread of these three runs, which is the strongest form this comparison can take while the other side is still a single draw - a difference the variance seen here does not explain, not a measured gap between two distributions. *** WHERE THIS RUNG SITS ON ITS OWN DIAL *** The same model at xhigh is 28.8 of 105 over four runs; this rung is 19.3 over three, a gap of +9.5. The dial as the board now shows it: low 11 (n=1), medium 30 (n=1), high 19.3 (n=3), xhigh 28.8 (n=4). For comparison Grok 4.6's dial ran low 15, medium 23, high 23, xhigh 28.7 - FLAT between medium and high, each of those from a single run. Whether that flatness is a property of the dial or a coincidence of two single draws is exactly what replicating these rungs was for. *** WHAT THE SPREAD ITSELF SAYS *** 5 points between the best and worst run of an IDENTICAL configuration - the three arms are clones and differ only in name. Any single-run number at this rung, including the one this row replaces, was carrying that much slack without being able to show it. Read any n=1 row on this board, from any vendor, with that in mind. *** COST AND TIME *** Reconstructed floors of $11.54, $12.02, $13.32 for a mean of $12.29; walls 40.5, 33.6, 39.6 minutes, mean 37.9. COST IS A FLOOR, not a bill: the grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates on the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis, and xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates. This row uses the per-session arithmetic corrected on 2026-09-21; on the older run-level arithmetic that the 4.6 rows on this board still use it would read $12.29. Compare cost across rows only where both use the same arithmetic. *** GENUINE EXTRAS *** Real defects found in the repo that are not part of the planted set ran 18, 15 and 14 across the three runs, a mean of 15.7. Extras are not scored; they are reported because a model that finds real bugs nobody planted is doing something the planted-bug total cannot see. *** THE TIER WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND AT THE LOWER RUNGS THAT MATTERS MOST *** A zero-token ACP readback before each of these three launches returned reasoning_effort high for a requested high, with the served model named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string AND its default is `high`, so a rung that failed to apply would look identical to one that worked in every artefact except that readback - the run would be a default-effort run wearing another label. The enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0. Legs SEQUENTIAL within every run, one repo at a time, and only one grok run on the machine at a time - two grok agents share one login. Sessions spawned per leg (repo 1 / repo 2): run 1 1 and 1; run 2 1 and 1; run 3 1 and 1. That count varies run to run on identical arm definitions for this model, tracks cost closely, and has tracked score not at all. The board's automatic regime check parses Claude Code transcripts, so it returns NOT CHECKED for every grok row here and the session counts above are the manual substitute. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at medium through xAI's own CLI, published as the MEAN OF THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 30, 23 and 27 of 105 (repo 1: 11, 11, 14 of 45 - repo 2: 19, 12, 13 of 60). Mean 26.7, spread 7. This supersedes the single-run row published earlier the same day at 30 of 105, which said the same thing on one draw. *** AGAINST THE PREVIOUS GENERATION AT THE SAME RUNG *** Grok 4.6 at medium scored 23 of 105 (7 on repo 1, 16 on repo 2) - A SINGLE RUN, so the samples are not the same size and the comparison is three draws against one. Difference +3.7. That 4.6 number falls INSIDE the spread of these three runs, which is the clearest way to say the two are not distinguishable on this evidence. *** WHERE THIS RUNG SITS ON ITS OWN DIAL *** The same model at xhigh is 28.8 of 105 over four runs; this rung is 26.7 over three, a gap of +2.1. The dial as the board now shows it: low 11 (n=1), medium 26.7 (n=3), high 19.3 (n=3), xhigh 28.8 (n=4). For comparison Grok 4.6's dial ran low 15, medium 23, high 23, xhigh 28.7 - FLAT between medium and high, each of those from a single run. Whether that flatness is a property of the dial or a coincidence of two single draws is exactly what replicating these rungs was for. *** WHAT THE SPREAD ITSELF SAYS *** 7 points between the best and worst run of an IDENTICAL configuration - the three arms are clones and differ only in name. Any single-run number at this rung, including the one this row replaces, was carrying that much slack without being able to show it. Read any n=1 row on this board, from any vendor, with that in mind. *** COST AND TIME *** Reconstructed floors of $25.15, $9.90, $15.25 for a mean of $16.77; walls 32.4, 27.1, 32.6 minutes, mean 30.7. COST IS A FLOOR, not a bill: the grok CLI reports context occupancy rather than cumulative usage, so every grok row here is reconstructed from the CLI's own session logs at xAI list rates on the same 2/0.5/6 per MTok basis, and xAI bills a request whose prompt reaches 200K at DOUBLE those rates. This row uses the per-session arithmetic corrected on 2026-09-21; on the older run-level arithmetic that the 4.6 rows on this board still use it would read $18.40. Compare cost across rows only where both use the same arithmetic. *** GENUINE EXTRAS *** Real defects found in the repo that are not part of the planted set ran 30, 16 and 22 across the three runs, a mean of 22.7. Extras are not scored; they are reported because a model that finds real bugs nobody planted is doing something the planted-bug total cannot see. *** THE TIER WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND AT THE LOWER RUNGS THAT MATTERS MOST *** A zero-token ACP readback before each of these three launches returned reasoning_effort medium for a requested medium, with the served model named by the session itself (currentModelId grok-4.7) rather than inferred from the -m flag, which has been inert on this bridge since it was probed on 2026-09-04. The grok CLI silently clamps an unknown effort string AND its default is `high`, so a rung that failed to apply would look identical to one that worked in every artefact except that readback - the run would be a default-effort run wearing another label. The enum grok-4.7 advertises is low, medium, high, xhigh. *** RECEIPTS *** All six legs exited 0. Legs SEQUENTIAL within every run, one repo at a time, and only one grok run on the machine at a time - two grok agents share one login. Sessions spawned per leg (repo 1 / repo 2): run 1 3 and 5; run 2 1 and 1; run 3 4 and 1. That count varies run to run on identical arm definitions for this model, tracks cost closely, and has tracked score not at all. The board's automatic regime check parses Claude Code transcripts, so it returns NOT CHECKED for every grok row here and the session counts above are the manual substitute. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5 on all six legs, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.value: OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol at max effort through OpenAI's own Codex CLI, on a ChatGPT account - the same auth path as every other Sol, Astra, Terra and Luna row here, NOT the metered API. 32 of 105: 18 of 45 on repo 1 and 14 of 60 on repo 2, 48 genuine extras, 60.4 minutes, $10.03. ONE RUN, measured the night the model shipped. *** THE NEWER CHECKPOINT DOES NOT LEAD ITS OWN FAMILY HERE *** GPT-6 Astra publishes 45 of 105 at max (mean of 3) and 43 at xhigh on this same benchmark; GPT-5.6 Sol publishes 43.5 at max (mean of 2). This row lands at 32, below all three, at a fraction of the cost - $10 against GPT-5.6 Sol's $95. A single run cannot settle a gap that size against a mean, but it is a large gap in the direction nobody would have guessed from the release order. *** IT KILLED AN ALL-TIME SURVIVOR *** one repo-1 bug, #6 in the public index, had outlived every model in every scored run on this board until now - a settings-persistence ordering defect, where a preference was written to storage before the change it described had actually taken effect, so a switch that failed or was dismissed left the stored value and the running session disagreeing. The survivor count drops from 32 to 31. That is worth separating from the score: this row sits in the middle of the table and still opened ground nothing above it had touched. It is also a variance event, not a capability - survivor kills on this board have not reproduced on demand in later runs. *** IT FINDS A LOT OF THINGS NOBODY PLANTED *** 48 genuine extras - real defects in the repos that are not part of the planted set - is among the highest counts on this board, from a row in the middle of the scoring table. Extras are reported separately and never folded into the score, but a model that flags this many unplanted defects while fixing fewer planted ones is spending its attention somewhere the planted total cannot see. *** THIS ROW RUNS A DIFFERENT CLI BUILD FROM EVERY OTHER OPENAI ROW, UNAVOIDABLY *** the Codex build the rest of this board uses (0.154.0) refuses this model outright - 'The gpt-6-sol model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account'. 0.155.1 runs it on the same account, same auth, same machine, so the blocker was the client and not entitlement. There is no version of this measurement that holds the harness fixed against the other OpenAI rows; the choice was a one-version harness delta or no row at all. Read the comparison above with that in it. (The rejection message is generic - a deliberately fake slug returns it verbatim - so it is not evidence about any model's existence.) *** THE FIRST TWO ATTEMPTS AT THIS ROW WERE VOID, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KNOWING *** the arm was first pinned to npm's shim rather than the real executable. On Windows that shim resolves to a .cmd, running a .cmd makes the shell re-parse the whole argument list, and a NEWLINE ENDS THE COMMAND - so the model received the benchmark prompt's first line, the repo description, and none of the numbered instructions. Both legs launched, billed and exited 0 with nothing to show the harness: one edited code and wrote no report it had never been asked for, the other replied asking what to work on. Nothing in the leg's own output said the prompt was short. Those legs are kept in the ledger, voided and labelled. This row is a clean re-run of both repos afterwards. A third earlier attempt died on an unrelated fault in the CLI's sandbox setup, since fixed. *** COST IS A LIST ESTIMATE AND A FLOOR *** token counts at OpenAI's published short-context rates, $2 input, $0.20 cached, $10 output per million. Requests over 272K input bill 2x on input and cache and 1.5x on output, which is NOT modelled here, so any leg that crossed that line cost more than this figure says. The Codex CLI on a subscription exposes no per-run bill, hence `list`, comparable only to other list rows. *** THE JUDGE IS NOT THIS BOARD'S DEFAULT, BY RULE *** a model may never judge itself or a sibling, and the default Codex judge is an OpenAI model, so it is disqualified for this arm - as is every other first-party GPT checkpoint here, since the rule is about shared weights and not identity-knowledge. Both legs were judged by grok-4.7 (the id is the one the scoring receipt records as SERVED, not the one the judge config asked for - from 2026-09-22 the endpoint has been resolving a request for grok-4.5 to grok-4.7, and notes published before 2026-09-23 named the requested id), blinded to the arm's identity. *** RECEIPTS *** Both legs exited 0 with a report written, run SEQUENTIALLY, one repo at a time. facts.value: OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol at max effort through OpenAI's own Codex CLI, on a ChatGPT account - the same auth path as every other Sol, Astra, Terra and Luna row here, NOT the metered API. Published as the MEAN OF TWO INDEPENDENT RUNS. Runs scored 32 and 30 of 105 (repo 1: 18, 16 of 45 - repo 2: 14, 14 of 60). Mean 31.0, spread 2. *** THIS SUPERSEDES GPT-6 SOL (MAX EFFORT) (32 OF 105) *** *** THE NEWER CHECKPOINT STILL DOES NOT LEAD ITS OWN FAMILY *** GPT-6 Astra publishes 45 of 105 at max (mean of 3) and 43 at xhigh on this same benchmark; GPT-5.6 Sol publishes 43.5 at max (mean of 2). This row lands at 31.0, below all three, at a fraction of the cost. The single run that first showed this was one draw on a board that has measured a 13-point spread between two runs of one identical max-effort configuration - which is exactly why it was replicated rather than left to stand. *** THE REPLICATES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE FIRST RUN *** same model string gpt-6-sol, same effort, same timeout, same pinned executable, same price table, same blind judge. Only the arm name differs, so the spread above is run-to-run variance and nothing else. *** IT FINDS A LOT OF THINGS NOBODY PLANTED *** 48 and 34 genuine extras across the runs, mean 41.0 - real defects in the repos that are not part of the planted set, among the highest counts on this board from a row in the middle of the scoring table. Extras are reported separately and never folded into the score, but a model that flags this many unplanted defects while fixing fewer planted ones is spending its attention somewhere the planted total cannot see. *** IT KILLED AN ALL-TIME SURVIVOR *** the first run fixed a planted bug that no scored pass by any model had ever fixed before - a settings-persistence ordering defect where the stored value is written before the live switch it is supposed to describe has landed. That is a first for this row and it stands regardless of where the mean settles. *** THIS ROW RUNS A DIFFERENT CLI BUILD FROM EVERY OTHER OPENAI ROW, UNAVOIDABLY *** the Codex build the rest of this board uses (0.154.0) refuses this model outright - 'The gpt-6-sol model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account'. 0.155.1 runs it on the same account, same auth, same machine, so the blocker was the client and not entitlement. There is no version of this measurement that holds the harness fixed against the other OpenAI rows; the choice was a one-version harness delta or no row at all. Read the comparison above with that in it. (The rejection message is generic - a deliberately fake slug returns it verbatim - so it is not evidence about any model's existence.) *** WALL AND COST *** Walls 60.4, 58.2 minutes, mean 59.3; cost $10.03, $8.17, mean $9.10. COST IS A LIST ESTIMATE AND A FLOOR - token counts at OpenAI's published short-context rates, $2 input, $0.20 cached, $10 output per million. Requests over 272K input bill 2x on input and cache and 1.5x on output, which is NOT modelled here, so any leg that crossed that line cost more than this figure says. The Codex CLI on a subscription exposes no per-run bill, hence `list`, comparable only to other list rows. *** THE JUDGE IS NOT THIS BOARD'S DEFAULT, BY RULE *** a model may never judge itself or a sibling, and the default Codex judge is an OpenAI model, so it is disqualified for this arm - as is every other first-party GPT checkpoint here, since the rule is about shared weights and not identity-knowledge. Legs were judged by grok-4.7 with a single exception - repo 1 of the second run drew grok-4.5 - blinded to the arm's identity. *** RECEIPTS *** All legs exited 0 with a report written, run SEQUENTIALLY, one repo at a time. The runs shared the laptop with legs from other vendors, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol at max effort through OpenAI's own Codex CLI, on a ChatGPT account - the same auth path as every other Sol, Astra, Terra and Luna row here, NOT the metered API. 44 of 105: 21 of 45 on repo 1 and 23 of 60 on repo 2, 59 genuine extras, 112.4 minutes, $6.56, 280 turns (133 and 147). ONE RUN, measured the night the model became reachable. For comparison the board publishes GPT-6 Sol at max 29.3 (mean of 3), GPT-6 Astra at max 45 (mean of 3), GPT-5.6 Sol at max 43.5 (mean of 2), Sonnet 5.5 at max 51.3 (mean of 3) of 105. *** MAX IS NOT THIS MODEL'S TOP TIER *** the account's own Codex model list offers low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra for gpt-6.1-sol - 'ultra' sits above max ('Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation'), so this row is not marked as the model's ceiling. *** THIS ROW RUNS A NEWER CODEX BUILD THAN THE OTHER OPENAI ROWS, UNAVOIDABLY *** the build the rest of this board's OpenAI rows use answers 'not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account' for this model on the same account at the same minute that Codex 0.159.0 runs it, so the blocker is the client, not entitlement. The GPT-6 Sol rows ran on 0.155.1, so a gap against them is model-plus-client. (That rejection message is generic - a made-up slug gets it word for word - so it is never evidence about whether a model exists; the API's own model list settled that.) *** AN EARLIER ATTEMPT IS VOIDED IN THE LEDGER *** Codex's sandbox was misconfigured on the machine and refused every command the model tried, so it never ran one; the runner marked it void (exit 90) and this row is a clean re-run. *** COST IS A LIST ESTIMATE *** token counts at OpenAI's published GPT-6.1 Sol short-context rates, $2 input, $0.10 cached, $10 output per million - half GPT-6 Sol's cached rate. Requests over 272K input bill 2x on input and cache and 1.5x on output; none of these legs sent one - Codex caps this model's context below that line, and the session records confirm every request stayed under it. The Codex CLI on a subscription exposes no per-run bill, hence `list`. *** THE JUDGE IS NOT THIS BOARD'S DEFAULT, BY RULE *** a model may never judge itself or a sibling, and the default Codex judge is an OpenAI model, so it is disqualified for this arm. Judged by grok-4.7, blinded to the arm's identity - the id is read back from the scoring receipt. *** RECEIPTS *** Both legs exited 0 with a report written, run SEQUENTIALLY, one repo at a time, code mode off as on the GPT-6 Sol arms. No other benchmark leg overlapped either leg - the only load this board's marker records - but the laptop was running several interactive coding-agent sessions that evening, at times near full CPU, so the wall figure may run high; scores, tokens and cost are unaffected.

facts.value: Grok 4.7 at xhigh through xAI's own CLI, published as the MEAN OF FIVE INDEPENDENT RUNS of one configuration. Runs scored 25, 30, 31, 29 and 30 of 105 (repo 1: 12, 12, 16, 12, 13 - repo 2: 13, 18, 15, 17, 17). Mean 29.0, range 6. *** THE FIFTH RUN CAME 17 DAYS LATER AND CHANGED NOTHING *** Runs 1-4 ran on 2026-09-21; run 5 on 2026-10-08, to test whether the model behind the grok-4.7 slug had improved since release. It scored 30, inside the first four's range, and moved the mean from 28.8 to 29.0. A clean run of an identical configuration is added to its row whatever it scores. Grok 4.6 at the same tier, a mean of three, stands at 28.7 of 105: the tie between the two generations holds at n=5. *** HOW RUN 5 WAS HELD TO THE SAME CONFIGURATION *** Same model, effort, prompt and judge, and the same CLI build as the first four (grok 1.0.30), run from a pinned copy because the installed CLI had auto-updated. The model was pinned per session and confirmed by the session itself. The context window needed restoring: by 2026-10-08 xAI's model metadata gave grok-4.7 a 256K default (500K optional), and the CLI reads it from there, so the run set 500K, the window runs 1-4 had and the size their prompts reached (~285K at peak). A zero-token readback before launch matched the 09-21 gate: grok-4.7, reasoning effort xhigh, 500,000-token window. *** WHAT DIFFERS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH *** Runs 1-4 took their two repos one after the other; run 5 took them at the same time, which is why this row's name drops 'seq'. That can only inflate run 5's wall, and run 5 was still the fastest of the five. Scores, tokens and cost are unaffected. Run 5's repo-2 leg was judged twice (a duplicate pass): 16 and 17 strict on the same diff. The board counts the newer pass, 17; the other would put the mean at 28.8. *** BUGS NOBODY PLANTED *** Genuine unplanted extras ran 26, 35, 34, 32 and 34 (mean 32.2). Reported separately and never added to the score. Claimed-only fixes: 0, 1, 0, 0 and 0. *** COST IS A RECONSTRUCTED FLOOR *** $16.55, $23.04, $29.93, $22.01 and $23.26 per run, mean $22.96, all on the same per-session arithmetic. The grok CLI reports context occupancy, not cumulative usage, so the cost is rebuilt from the CLI's own session logs at xAI's API list rates ($2 / $0.50 / $6 per MTok). It is a floor: checked on run 5 against exact token counts, it sat about 10% under list before xAI's double rate on prompts of 200K and up, which these runs reach and this method cannot see. *** THE TIER IS THE MODEL CEILING *** A zero-token readback before every launch returned reasoning effort xhigh; grok-4.7 advertises low, medium, high and xhigh, so nothing above xhigh exists to ask for. *** RECEIPTS *** All ten legs exited 0. Per-run wall 39.6, 47.3, 51.8, 45.4, 39.4 minutes. 6 of the 10 legs shared the laptop with another arm and the rest had it to themselves, which the wall marker discloses per leg - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

facts.about: Gemini 4 Argon (high effort, Antigravity CLI) - mean of 3
facts.value: Google's Gemini 4 Argon at thinking level high - its top tier - through the Antigravity CLI, Google's current agent CLI. MEAN OF THREE RUNS: 40, 45 and 37 of 105 (repo 1: 14, 13 and 12 of 45 - repo 2: 26, 32 and 25 of 60), mean 40.7. Genuine unplanted extras 4, 7 and 11; claimed-only fixes 1, 0 and 2. Walls 37.4, 47.3 and 84.7 minutes; cost $5.74, $6.43 and $9.30 at list, from Google's per-call usage (agy's own token counts read 10-38% lower and were used when this row was first published; corrected 2026-10-14). *** THE SAME MODEL IN GEMINI CLI *** scored 33 in one run at the same thinking level, for $32.08 in 85.1 minutes - kept as its own row. Same model, same tier, same judge. The score gap is all on repo 2, and the Gemini CLI side is a single run while these three spread 8 points (37 to 45), so it is not established as a harness effect. The cost gap is mechanical: Gemini CLI re-sent its whole conversation on every call (44M prompt tokens, 69% cached) and cost about 4.5 times as much. *** HOW ANTIGRAVITY REACHED ARGON *** The Antigravity CLI does not list Argon on a Google AI Pro subscription. Its enterprise gateway mode lists it, signed in with a Gemini API key; a local gateway passes requests through unchanged and presents the key the way the Gemini API expects. The CLI itself sends thinkingLevel HIGH for gemini-4-argon-high, and every request was served by gemini-4-argon. *** EFFORT high IS THE CEILING *** The API accepts low, medium and high for this model and rejects max and ultra. *** COST *** a list estimate from Google's per-call usage at its launch rate ($2 input / $0.10 cached input / $10 output per million tokens, thinking billed as output); 89% of prompt tokens were cache reads. If Google bills prompts over 200K tokens at a higher rate, as it does for its Pro models, this figure and the Gemini CLI row's are low. *** RUN 2 WAS RESUMED *** Both of its legs stopped when the API key's prepaid credit ran out, without a report; after a top-up each continued its own conversation and finished. Its wall is the two segments' sum with the idle gap removed. *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock. Judge: blind Codex gpt-5.5, which is neither this model nor a sibling of it.

The two tiers are level on repo 1; high leads on repo 2 on average, and medium costs about the same per run. Its wall is the two segments' sum. *** COST *** a list estimate from Google's per-call usage at its launch rate ($2 input / $0.10 cached input / $10 output per million tokens); legs that ran together are split by agy's per-leg share. If Google bills prompts over 200K tokens at a higher rate, as it does for its Pro models, this figure is low. *** RECEIPTS *** 5 of the 6 legs shared the laptop with another arm and the rest had it to themselves, which the wall marker discloses per leg - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock. ONE RUN: 32 of 105 - 12 of 45 on repo 1 and 20 of 60 on repo 2 - with 1 partial fix(es), 0 claimed-only and 3 genuine unplanted extras; 44.9 minutes, $5.97. Medium stands at 39.3 and high at 40.7 (means of three); low is the cheapest tier by a little, not by much. *** WHY ONE RUN *** Three low runs were started. In runs 1 and 3 the repo-2 leg did not finish: twice the local gateway stopped answering before Google started its stream (the CLI gives up on a response that has not begun within about a minute), and the resumed conversations then hit the API key's depleted prepaid credit. Run 2 completed both repos and is the row. *** A DIFFERENT JUDGE *** this row was judged by Grok (grok-4.7), not Codex gpt-5.5 like the other Argon rows: from about 16:56 on Oct 14 Codex refused gpt-5.5 for the account. facts.value: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at effort max in DEEPSEEK HARNESS (dsh 0.2.1-rc.2, DeepSeek's own agent), on the same model id (deepseek-flash) and the same DeepSeek endpoint (Anthropic Messages, output_config.effort) as the Claude Code rows - the harness is the variable. MEAN OF 7 RUNS: 42, 41, 47, 47, 40, 43 and 39 of 105 (repo 1: 19, 18, 19, 20, 16, 20 and 21 of 45 - repo 2: 23, 23, 28, 27, 24, 23 and 18 of 60), mean 42.7. Genuine unplanted extras 44, 42, 40, 39, 46, 51 and 46; claimed-only fixes 1, 2, 0, 1, 3, 0 and 0. Active minutes 71.2, 60.8, 62.8, 69.0, 58.6, 51.1 and 61.0; cost $2.28, $1.67, $1.40, $1.74, $2.15, $1.98 and $1.68. *** AGAINST CLAUDE CODE *** the same model at max in Claude Code stands at 39.1 (its own row): +3.6 here. With runs this spread the gap is a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** headless profile with a JSON event stream; web search and fetch switched off (no internet during a run, as for every harness here); subagents on as shipped; permission mode danger-full-access, the equivalent of every other harness's skip-permissions flag; a fresh dsh home per leg; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). *** THE FIRST HARNESS RUN WAS VOIDED *** at max it read the upstream project's git history on repo 1 and diffed it against its working copy; asked directly, it confirmed it. That run is excluded and was replaced. *** 5 OF 7 RUNS RAN IN SEGMENTS *** DeepSeek's balance-based concurrency cap (429) and then the prepaid balance running out (402) stopped those legs before they wrote a report; after a top-up each continued its own dsh session to the end (one leg also lost a response stream and continued again). Their time counts active work only, each segment from its first to its last successful model call; tokens and cost sum every segment. The resumed segments, and every later run, carried a retry policy for rate limits and dropped streams, which changes no model behaviour. *** EFFORT max *** read on the wire for every request: 7,108 of 7,123 requests carried max; the rest are dsh's own housekeeping calls (a no-effort side call per leg; one context-condensing call at high). *** COST IS A REAL BILL AT OFF-PEAK RATES *** DeepSeek's own per-call usage at its off-peak list price (a weekend); the account balance moved by the same amount within 1%. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** 4 of the 14 legs shared the laptop with another arm and the rest had it to themselves, which the wall marker discloses per leg - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

Pi uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint where the other two use the Anthropic-compatible one. Planned as n=7, cut to n=5 for budget before the sixth run. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at effort high in PI (pi-coding-agent 1.3.0, Earendil's open-source minimal coding agent), on the same model id (deepseek-flash) and DeepSeek account as the Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness rows - the harness is the variable. Pi uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint where the other two use the Anthropic-compatible one. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 40, 39, 41, 38 and 44 of 105 (repo 1: 18, 14, 15, 13 and 20 of 45 - repo 2: 22, 25, 26, 25 and 24 of 60), mean 40.4. Genuine unplanted extras 36, 34, 23, 17 and 37; claimed-only fixes 2, 0, 0, 0 and 2. Minutes 57.7, 51.8, 48.3, 40.8 and 43.1; cost $0.64, $0.83, $0.68, $0.44 and $0.62. *** AGAINST THE OTHER HARNESSES *** the same model at high stands at 36.4 in Claude Code and 39.2 in DeepSeek Harness (means of 5, their own rows); Pi at max: 42.2: +4.0 over Claude Code, at a lower cost per run than either. Pi runs no subagents, so whatever lifts it above Claude Code is not subagents. With runs this spread the gaps are a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** print mode with a JSON event stream; built-in tools only (read, bash, edit, write) - Pi ships no subagents and no web tools; extensions, skills, MCP and prompt templates off; a fresh Pi config directory per leg; the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loads as Pi's context file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). Every leg ran in one segment. *** EFFORT high *** read on the wire for every request: 1,637 of 1,637 carried reasoning_effort=high (Pi's catalog maps --thinking high to high for this model). *** COST IS A REAL BILL AT OFF-PEAK RATES *** DeepSeek's own per-call usage at its off-peak list price (a weekend); the account balance moved by the same amount. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at effort max in OPENCODE (opencode-ai 1.19.3, the open-source coding agent), on the same model id (deepseek-flash) and DeepSeek account as the Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness and Pi rows - the harness is the variable. OpenCode uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, like Pi. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 36, 40, 35, 38 and 39 of 105 (repo 1: 13, 17, 18, 15 and 16 of 45 - repo 2: 23, 23, 17, 23 and 23 of 60), mean 37.6. Genuine unplanted extras 33, 37, 43, 36 and 32; claimed-only fixes 1, 0, 0, 0 and 0. Minutes 58.8, 41.9, 73.1, 49.8 and 55.1; cost $1.01, $0.75, $1.23, $0.76 and $1.04. *** AGAINST THE OTHER HARNESSES *** the same model at max stands at 39.1 in Claude Code, 42.7 in DeepSeek Harness and 42.2 in Pi (means of 7, 7 and 5, their own rows). OpenCode's best run (40) sits below every Pi run (41-44) and at the bottom of DeepSeek Harness's range (39-47), so at max it trails both; against Claude Code (34-46) the ranges overlap and the gap is a lean. *** SETUP *** `opencode run` with a JSON event stream; tools as shipped, including its task tool for subagents (it started 1 subagent across the ten legs, 154 of the 2,382 requests), except web fetch and web search, which are off; a fresh OpenCode config and data home per leg; its Claude-Code compatibility layer off and the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loaded explicitly as an instruction file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). Every leg ran in one segment. OpenCode's stream reports no context accounting, but the tap's per-request prompt sizes show the main loop's context only ever grew (peak 803K tokens of the 1M window), so no leg compacted. Generated test-coverage reports were left out of the judged diff (generated output, never a fix). A first attempt at max was discarded unjudged - a launch fault made OpenCode work outside the run folders - and all ten legs were rerun with the fault fixed; these are the rerun's numbers. *** EFFORT max *** read on the wire: 2,372 of 2,382 requests carried reasoning_effort=max; the other 10 were OpenCode's own short session-title calls, which it sends at low whatever the variant. *** COST IS A REAL BILL AT OFF-PEAK RATES *** DeepSeek's own per-call usage at its off-peak list price (the runs fell in its off-peak window: a Sunday); the account balance moved by the same amount. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

facts.value: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at effort high in OPENCODE (opencode-ai 1.19.3, the open-source coding agent), on the same model id (deepseek-flash) and DeepSeek account as the Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness and Pi rows - the harness is the variable. OpenCode uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, like Pi. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 35, 37, 43, 28 and 40 of 105 (repo 1: 14, 15, 18, 14 and 16 of 45 - repo 2: 21, 22, 25, 14 and 24 of 60), mean 36.6. Genuine unplanted extras 11, 45, 24, 19 and 29; claimed-only fixes 0, 1, 1, 1 and 2. Minutes 28.7, 63.7, 53.6, 25.5 and 36.7; cost $0.43, $1.12, $1.17, $0.53 and $0.69. *** AGAINST THE OTHER HARNESSES *** the same model at high stands at 36.4 in Claude Code, 39.2 in DeepSeek Harness and 40.4 in Pi (means of 5, their own rows). OpenCode is level with Claude Code and below the other two, but its runs (28-43) overlap all three ranges (Claude Code 30-42, DeepSeek Harness 32-45, Pi 38-44), so at high the gaps are a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** `opencode run` with a JSON event stream; tools as shipped, including its task tool for subagents (it started 8 subagents across the ten legs, 726 of the 2,241 requests), except web fetch and web search, which are off; a fresh OpenCode config and data home per leg; its Claude-Code compatibility layer off and the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loaded explicitly as an instruction file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). Every leg ran in one segment. OpenCode's stream reports no context accounting, but the tap's per-request prompt sizes show the main loop's context only ever grew (peak 669K tokens of the 1M window), so no leg compacted. Generated test-coverage reports were left out of the judged diff (generated output, never a fix). *** EFFORT high *** read on the wire: 2,231 of 2,241 requests carried reasoning_effort=high; the other 10 were OpenCode's own short session-title calls, which it sends at low whatever the variant. *** COST IS A REAL BILL AT OFF-PEAK RATES *** DeepSeek's own per-call usage at its off-peak list price (the runs fell in its off-peak window: late Sunday UTC); the account balance moved by the same amount. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

Pi uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint where the other two use the Anthropic-compatible one. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 37, 38, 32, 37 and 25 of 105 (repo 1: 16, 15, 14, 14 and 11 of 45 - repo 2: 21, 23, 18, 23 and 14 of 60), mean 33.8. Pi runs no subagents, so whatever lifts it above Claude Code is not subagents. With runs this spread the gaps are a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** print mode with a JSON event stream; built-in tools only (read, bash, edit, write) - Pi ships no subagents and no web tools; extensions, skills, MCP and prompt templates off; a fresh Pi config directory per leg; the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loads as Pi's context file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). facts.quote: id: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (low effort, Pi) - mean of 5 | note: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at effort low in PI (pi-coding-agent 1.3.0, Earendil's open-source minimal coding agent), on the same model id (deepseek-flash) and DeepSeek account as the Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness rows - the harness is the variable. Pi uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint where the other two use the Anthropic-compatible one. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 37, 38, 32, 37 and 25 of 105 (repo 1: 16, 15, 14, 14 and 11 of 45 - repo 2: 21, 23, 18, 23 and 14 of 60), mean 33.8. Genuine unplanted extras 21, 16, 16, 26 and 19; claimed-only fixes 3, 0, 2, 0 and 0. Minutes 39.4, 31.2, 28.8, 34.6 and 32.1; cost $0.54, $0.41, $0.35, $0.53 and $0.46. *** AGAINST THE OTHER HARNESSES *** the same model at low stands at 34.4 in Claude Code and 34.8 in DeepSeek Harness (means of 5, their own rows); Pi at high: 40.4, at max: 42.2: -0.6 over Claude Code, at a lower cost per run than either. Pi runs no subagents, so whatever lifts it above Claude Code is not subagents. With runs this spread the gaps are a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** print mode with a JSON event stream; built-in tools only (read, bash, edit, write) - Pi ships no subagents and no web tools; extensions, skills, MCP and prompt templates off; a fresh Pi config directory per leg; the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loads as Pi's context file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). Every leg ran in one segment. *** EFFORT low *** read on the wire for every request: 1,204 of 1,204 carried reasoning_effort=low (Pi's catalog maps --thinking low to low for this model). Run 5 scored 25 in a normal run (about 16 minutes per repo, 125 and 180 tool calls) - a weak run, not a failure; the median of the five is 37. *** COST IS A REAL BILL AT OFF-PEAK RATES *** DeepSeek's own per-call usage at its off-peak list price (a weekend); the account balance moved by the same amount. *** JUDGE *** Grok (grok-4.7). *** RECEIPTS *** Every leg shared the laptop with another arm, which the wall marker discloses - scores, tokens and cost are untouched by that, only the clock.

OpenCode uses DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, like Pi. MEAN OF 5 RUNS: 36, 32, 27, 31 and 38 of 105 (repo 1: 22, 12, 12, 13 and 20 of 45 - repo 2: 14, 20, 15, 18 and 18 of 60), mean 32.8. Genuine unplanted extras 25, 12, 9, 9 and 33; claimed-only fixes 1, 1, 1, 1 and 4. Minutes 49.0, 31.9, 26.2, 31.3 and 67.6; cost $0.90, $0.38, $0.41, $0.53 and $1.10. *** AGAINST THE OTHER HARNESSES *** the same model at low stands at 34.4 in Claude Code, 34.8 in DeepSeek Harness and 33.8 in Pi (means of 5, their own rows). OpenCode is the lowest of the four, but its runs (27-38) overlap all three ranges (Claude Code 32-40, DeepSeek Harness 34-36, Pi 25-38), so at low the gaps are a lean, not an established difference. *** SETUP *** `opencode run` with a JSON event stream; tools as shipped, including its task tool for subagents (it started 13 subagents across the ten legs, 1,030 of the 2,465 requests), except web fetch and web search, which are off; a fresh OpenCode config and data home per leg; its Claude-Code compatibility layer off and the run repo's own CLAUDE.md loaded explicitly as an instruction file; the integrity warning appended to the task in every run (work only inside this folder; anything outside is cheating and every tool call is checked). Generated test-coverage reports were left out of the judged diff (generated output, never a fix).
